Perch asks, optionally, for citizenship status and state of residence on both sides. Code compares them with a listing's own quoted rule in a few closed phrases. Findings so far

  • No NSF back-test: Grants.gov's NSF archive has almost no listings that opened 2015 to 2021, and 291 archived NSF listings carry a bulk open date of 2025-06-06. A date cut-off cannot be applied, so NSF PIs get a hand check on current listings.
  • Flaky test: tests/test_scout.py::test_route_b_answer_counts_and_dates_pass_the_validator failed once in a full run and passed alone and on two reruns.
  • Public CVs and group pages: Dakshitha allowed them as test input. Any such text stays in the session scratchpad, never in the repo.
  • SBIR.gov API: still 403 on 2026-10-30 for awards, firm and solicitations; the API page still says it is under maintenance.
  • DOE Office of Science: it files under the Grants.gov code PAMS-SC, not DOE-SC, so a first check by code found nothing. Its annual open call, DE-FOA-0003665, is posted and closes 2027-09-30.
  • Institution-level programs: cancer center grants, SPOREs, NSF GRANTED and CREST still reach some top 10s (Q39).
  • Eligibility rules added: Young Investigator and Young Faculty titles count as career stage; programs for primarily undergraduate or undergraduate-focused institutions are dropped; EPSCoR and DEPSCoR are dropped unless the record names Pennsylvania (NSF list frozen through FY2027, read 2026-10-30).
  • Hand check before the new rules (R0): the program behind each NSF PI's latest award ranked 1 or 2: MPS Chemistry first for PI-130 and PI-131, MPS Physics second for PI-132 and first for PI-133. The DOE Office of Science call ranked first for PI-132.

Definition of done

  • Dakshitha closes the session.

Reviews and QA cycles, newest first

UX

Newest: docs/design/S51_DESIGN.md, last changed 5 Nov 2026, 06:51. May be behind: older than the start of S54 (5 Nov 2026, 10:25)

S51 design: round 3 build spec (2026-11-05)docs/design/S51_DESIGN.md, 5 Nov 2026

This spec turns the three round 3 reviews into one last build before the release. It reuses the S50 conventions: the walk-flow loader, the package rules in S50_DESIGN.md section 3.1, the S49 rules that section points to, and the shared-contract style ("A styles it; A and B emit it").

Item codes refer to these documents:

  • W1 to W39: S51_UIUX_REVIEW.md.
  • D1 to D33: S51_PRODUCT_REVIEW.md.
  • H1 to H20: S51_FUNCTION_REVIEW.md.
  • LIVE: the real-model capture in build/s50_live/LIVE.md.

The walk researcher is PI-4 (A5026494099). The live capture is PI-1 (A5063022331). No other researcher is named here.

1. Decisions

The orchestrator records each of these in docs/DECISIONS.md when the spec is accepted.

  • Centre and programme grants get their own group (H7, D3, decided 2026-11-05):
    • The field: Lead.group widens to Literal["temple_internal", "centre"].
    • The route: a centre lead stays on route A. routeOf in web/app.js already maps only temple_internal to the Temple tab, so it needs no change.
    • Which codes: exactly P30, P01, P50 and U54, read from opportunity.activity_code. The builder does not add codes from memory. Adding any other code needs NIH's public activity-codes page read first, with its URL recorded in docs/SOURCES.md. That is after release.
    • What stays the same: rank and match_score do not change, and neither does the Match pill. Inside the group, the cards keep the list's own order.
    • The fold: the front end draws these leads in a fold named "Centre and programme grants (N)". It sits below the single-lab cards and below the "Show N more" fold.
  • Accounts can be marked closed (D4, D5):
    • The setting: a new setting, PERCH_ACCOUNTS_OPEN, defaults to 1. The orchestrator sets it to 0 in .env.deploy when it updates the deploy, because self-registration is off there.
    • The field: /auth/session returns it as accounts_open.
    • What changes on screen: while accounts are closed, the landing's second button starts the guest sample. The Scout and hand-off walls also lead with the example.
    • What stays: the header's quiet "Sign in" link, so the presenter can still sign in.
  • The fit verdict goes on the researcher card's face (W13):
    • The face: the model's inference sentence now sits right under the facts, labelled "Why it fits:" or "How it relates:", with the "Inference" tag.
    • The disclosure: the "what the call funds" sentence moves inside it.
    • Which cards start open: with a CV in the brief, only the first card starts open (W14). This revises the S27 rule that every card starts open.
    • The reason: the verdict is now on every card's face.
  • One paper per "you" sentence in cover points (H1):
    • The rule: a you sentence that cites papers must cite exactly one.
    • Where it is checked: the cover skill's validate. A sentence that cites two or more fails, and the set is regenerated once, as rule 5 says.
  • A name-only student listing gets no model call (H4, D6):
    • Which listings: an empty purpose, empty eligibility.notes and an empty field_of_study.
    • What the card shows: a code-written line in lead.notes, not in explanation. So the card never calls it model text.
  • Student entry labels (H9, W20, D14):
    • One entry: the label is "Your entry".
    • Several entries: each is "One of your entries".
    • The interests note: "Your interests note".
    • The sample student: the labels read "the sample student's" in place of "your".
  • The precache key carries a rules version (H8): the key gets RULES_VERSION = "2026-11-05.1" from perch/eligibility.py. Every later change to a rule bumps it.
  • The sample's canary tokens are hidden in the boxes (W3, D17; DECISIONS 2026-11-05, revised): "Load sample" fills the boxes without the canary line. Save adds it back, so the stored text keeps it.
  • The guest budget line (D16):
    • When it shows: when a brief's explanation stage was skipped by the model budget.
    • Where: one line above the list, on both sides.
    • How the front end knows: it reads the stage's own detail, which code writes as BUDGET_DETAIL. No new field is added. A back-end test pins the text.
  • Run again shows once (W5):
    • While building: the header's "Run again" is hidden while the brief is queued or running.
    • After a stop: it is also hidden after the user stopped the brief, because the progress card shows its own.
    • On My Perch: the order is Open, Run again, Stop (W12).
  • One name for one order (W8): the compare sort's first option reads "Best match".
  • W26 is dropped: on the deploy every model role is Anthropic. loop.py:687 therefore sets where="cloud", and the tag already reads "Cloud: Anthropic". The review's wording, "Perch's own server", would be false.

For Dakshitha

  • D9, whose name goes on the projector:
    • The risk: a live researcher brief shows a real Temple researcher's name, and its hand-off is written in that person's first person. Nothing records that the person agreed to appear on stage.
    • Recommendation: for the researcher side on stage, present the aliased example (example.html). If Dakshitha has a researcher who has agreed, present that person's brief instead. Do not search a stranger's name live.
    • Effect on this spec: none. It changes the run sheet only.

2. Scope for round 3

The cap is about 3 hours of builder time, for three builders in parallel. Tier A is the must-fix work and ships. Tier B is ranked polish and ships only under budget, cut from the bottom.

  • Tier A is about 230 minutes of builder time, about 50 over the cap:
    • The packages: BE about 110 minutes, FE-A about 65 and FE-B about 55.
    • Wall-clock: with three builders in parallel, this is about 2 hours, and BE is the binding package.
    • The must-fix list alone: the review estimates for H1, H4, H5, H7, H8 and H9 add up to about 5 hours. The scopes below are the smallest safe versions of each.
  • What the cuts remove: cuts 1, 5 and 6 are polish. Cuts 2, 3 and 4 remove must-fix work. They are offered only because the must-fix set alone is over the cap.
  • The next polish cut: if BE runs long, W19 (the unsupported fold) is the next one. It is Tier A in both front-end packages, but it is not a must-fix.
  • The cut line, to reach about 180 minutes. Cut in this order:
    • FE-A, W13: the card keeps "what it funds" on its face. This saves 15 minutes.
    • BE, W7's instrument row: keep the "no written reason" wording, and leave the row in. This saves 5 minutes.
    • FE-B, W12: My Perch rows keep their current order. This saves 8 minutes.
    • BE, H9: the front end's W20 mapping still fixes the id form, but titles stay "Your achievement A" in the model text. This saves 10 minutes.
    • FE-A, the D16 line on the researcher side: the student side keeps it, since that is the audience path. This saves 5 minutes.
    • FE-B, help: help keeps only the centre-grant sentence and the budget sentence. This saves 6 minutes.

Must-fix coverage

  • UI/UX review:
    • W1 and W2 are A1.
    • W3 is B1.
    • W4, W5 and W6 are A2.
    • W7 is BE7.
    • W8 is B4.
    • W9 is B4.
    • W10 and W11 are A1.
    • W12 is B5.
  • Product review:
    • D1 is the release session; see section 3.6.
    • D2 is H1.
    • D3 is BE2 and A3.
    • D4 is BE8 and A4.
    • D5 is B2.
    • D6 is BE3, with the ordering question in Limits.
    • D7 and D8 are run-sheet steps for the orchestrator.
    • D9 is for Dakshitha, above.
    • D10 is the release docs: the README "See it" line and tracking the student example.
  • Function review:
    • H1 is BE1.
    • H4 is BE3.
    • H5 is BE4.
    • H7 is BE2.
    • H8 is BE5.
    • H9 is BE6.
    • H2, the re-capture, is the orchestrator's after the merge, with again=true and a new idempotency option.
    • H3 is done by the decision that raised the guest budget.
    • H6 is BE Tier B.

Deferred, with reasons

  • W14's line clamp: W13 moves the long sentence into the disclosure, so the clamp is not needed. Only the "first card open" half ships, in A3.
  • W15 to W19, W21 to W25 and W27 to W34: these are Tier B in their packages, in rank order. What does not ship goes nowhere: none of them is a limit a user meets.
  • W26: dropped (section 1).
  • W35 to W39 and D26 to D33: both reviews date these after Demo Day.
  • D11 and D12, Scout's tails and mixed lists: these touch the Scout prompt, and a prompt change needs a paid bench to check. They go in Limits.
  • D13, expiry shown as a deadline: the researcher card already labels an expiry "Announcement" (web/app.js, the expires branch). QA checks the P01 card after H2's re-capture. It is not built.
  • D18, old Temple calls: S50's G5 rule should already leave them out. QA checks after H2.
  • D19, industry ids: QA checks the CSV, the JSON export and the compare table after H2.
  • D20, the same papers on most cards: not measured since 3b landed (H14). It goes in Limits.
  • D21, awards list order: it needs a server sort parameter. It goes in Limits.
  • D25, Run again next to Export: the presenter avoids it. It goes in Limits.
  • H13, Scout headings, and H12, cover wording: these are BE Tier B.
  • H15, the free Scout replay: the orchestrator runs it on CPU after BE merges, through scripts/run_limited.sh.

3. Build packages

3.0 Step 0, done by the orchestrator before any builder starts (about 5 minutes, one commit)

  • Walk flow files: create scripts/walk_flows/s51_fe_a.py and s51_fe_b.py. Each holds def register(U): return {}, [].
  • Who owns which flow file:
    • FE-A: s51_fe_a.py, s50_fe_a.py and s49_fe_a.py.
    • FE-B: s51_fe_b.py, s50_fe_b.py, s50_fe_c.py, s49_fe_b.py and s49_be_s.py.
  • The walk server: start it with PERCH_SCHEDULER=0, as in S50.
  • No other shared file is touched in Step 0. Each contract in 3.2 is read with a safe default, so each package works before the others merge.

3.1 Rules for every package

S50_DESIGN.md section 3.1 applies unchanged: isolation, fail first, one walk server on port 8191 through scripts/run_limited.sh, worktrees without the example files, and stubs for missing contracts. Three additions:

  • Walk checks are lean: at most six new checks per front-end package. Each one is listed below. Each must fail on the branch before the change, and the builder notes the failing value in the hand-back.
  • Old checks this round breaks on purpose: the builder lists them in the hand-back, and the orchestrator edits scripts/ux_walk.py after the merge. These are known now:
    • The weak fold's summary text: it now reads "Show N more" (A3).
    • The compare sort's first option text: it now reads "Best match" (B4).
    • The My Perch link text: "Change details and run again" now reads "Run again" (B5).
    • Any check that expects "Canary:" in a Load sample box: the line is hidden now (B1).
  • The back-end builder runs make test. It does not run the walk. Each front-end builder runs tests/test_web.py and its own walk flows.

3.2 Shared contracts

Lead group for centre grants (BE builds it; FE-A reads it)
{"id": "...", "route": "A", "group": "centre", "rank": 1, "match_score": 82,
 "notes": ["Centre or programme grant (activity code P30). An institution applies for these for a centre or a group of projects, so Perch lists them below the single-lab grants."],
 "opportunity": {"activity_code": "P30", "...": "..."}}
  • The note: BE writes it, with the code filled in from the record. FE-A shows it through leadNotes, as it already does for every note.
  • The default: a lead without group is a single-lab card.
Accounts open (BE builds it; FE-A reads it and passes it on; FE-B reads it from ctx)
  • GET /auth/session: every response shape (signed out, guest and signed in) gains "accounts_open": true|false.
  • FE-A: adds accountsOpen: S.session.accounts_open !== false to every ctx object it builds:
    • the Scout ctx at web/app.js:1365;
    • the hand-off ctx at :1355;
    • coverCtx() at :2100;
    • the student ctx passed to studentRoutes at :1341.
  • FE-B: reads ctx.accountsOpen !== false. A missing field means open, so nothing changes before the merge.
The budget line (FE-A emits it on the researcher list; FE-B emits it on the student list; FE-A styles it)
  • When it shows: the brief's explanations stage (researcher) or student_explanations stage (student) has status: "skipped", and its detail starts with "withheld: the daily model budget".
  • Markup: p.notice.info.list-note[data-budget] with icon("info") and this text: "Written reasons are paused: this session’s model budget for today is used. The list, dates, amounts and rule results are not affected."
  • Where it goes: in the list's notices slot, first in the slot. When it shows, the withheld-reason note does not.
The unsupported-sentence fold (FE-A styles it; FE-A and FE-B emit it) (W19, Tier A for both)
details.unsupported-fold
  summary[data-key=unsupported]   "1 sentence could not be matched to its source" / "N sentences could not …"
  ul > li (each sentence, as it came)
  • What it replaces: the amber div.notice.warn on the researcher card (web/app.js, in explanationBlock) and on the student card (web/student.js:487).
  • CSS (FE-A, styles.css): .unsupported-fold summary { color: var(--ink-2); font-size: var(--fs-14, 14px); min-height: 44px; display: flex; align-items: center; } .unsupported-fold ul { margin: 4px 0 0; padding-left: 20px; color: var(--ink-2); }.

3.3 Package BE: back end (Tier A about 110 minutes)

Files BE may touch:

  • perch/skills/cover.py
  • perch/validate.py
  • perch/eligibility.py
  • perch/precache.py
  • perch/service.py
  • perch/student.py
  • perch/skills/fit.py
  • perch/schemas.py (the Lead.group literal only)
  • perch/compare.py
  • perch/auth/routes.py
  • perch/config.py
  • .env.example
  • the cover prompt file, if it is not in cover.py
  • new tests/test_s51_*.py
  • existing tests that pin a string this package changes

BE must not edit: web/, scripts/, the docs/ files, .env or .env.deploy.

Escalate instead of guessing:

  • a database or JSON-schema constraint on group;
  • a back-test path that reads group or the brief's display order;
  • a skill test that needs a paid call.
BE1. H1: one paper per "you" sentence (30 minutes)
  • Validate: in validate (perch/skills/cover.py:348), a you point whose citations hold two or more paper ids (W…) fails, with the reason "cites more than one paper; name one paper and one fact".
  • Prompt: "Each ‘you’ point names one paper and one fact from it, as ‘Your paper reports …’. Do not add a judgment after it, such as ‘which shows …’."
  • YOU_SUBJECT (:255): it also matches your papers?.
  • as_record_claim: turns "You have" into "The paper has", and "Your paper(s) report(s)" into "The paper reports".
  • Tests:
    • "Your paper reports X" becomes "The paper reports X".
    • "You have work on X" becomes "The paper has work on X".
    • A two-paper point fails validate with the reason above.
    • A one-paper point passes.
  • Not in this round: the optional link field.
BE2. H7: centre and programme grants (25 minutes)
  • perch/eligibility.py: add CENTRE_CODES = frozenset({"P30", "P01", "P50", "U54"}), with a comment that points to this spec.
  • Where the group is set: where route A leads are built in perch/service.py, set lead.group = "centre" for each lead whose opportunity.activity_code is in the set. Append the note from 3.2. Do it on the fresh path and on the precache path; the Temple internal group is computed live at service.py:456, so follow that pattern.
  • What it must not change: rank, match_score and explanation.
  • The back-test: confirm that bench/ reads rank, not the group or the shown order, and say so in the hand-back. The orchestrator re-runs the back-test in the release session.
  • Tests:
    • A P30 lead gets group: "centre" and the note, and its rank is unchanged.
    • An R01 lead gets no group.
    • A Temple internal lead keeps temple_internal.
BE3. H4: name-only student listings (15 minutes)
  • In _run_student_explanations (perch/service.py:706): leave out of explain_leads every lead whose scholarship has all three of these:
    • an empty purpose, after the canary tail is removed;
    • empty eligibility.notes;
    • an empty field_of_study.

    • It sets PERCH_ACCOUNTS_OPEN=0 in .env.deploy.
    • It runs H2's re-capture with a new idempotency option and again=true for cover points.
    • It runs H15's free replay.
    • QA runs the full walk at 1280 and 360, in light and dark, and opens every changed screenshot.
    • QA checks D13, D18 and D19 on the re-capture.
  6. The release session (S52):
    • re-export both example files (A6);
    • re-run the back-test;
    • D7's morning run sheet;
    • D8's port test;
    • D10's README line;
    • copy section 5 into the README's Known limits.

4. Help changes (web/help.js, FE-B)

Every sentence must be true of the merged code.

  • Centre and programme grants: "Centre and programme grants, such as a P30 or a P01, sit in their own fold under the single-lab grants. An institution applies for these. Their Match number does not change."
  • The card's face: "Each grant card shows the model’s reading of the fit under the dates: Why it fits, or How it relates for a weaker match. It is marked Inference. Open the card for what the call funds and the papers it cites."
  • Match: "The Match number ranks the leads. The text says why. It is not the odds of funding."
  • Sentences not matched to a source: "When a sentence could not be matched to its source, the card says so in a small fold that lists it."
  • A paused budget: "When this session’s model budget for the day is used, written reasons pause. One line above the list says so. The list, dates, amounts and rule results are not affected."
  • Name-only listings: "When a Temple listing gives only an award’s name, the card says so and points to its page. No model writes a reason for it."
  • The example: "While accounts are not open, Ask Scout and the note to the office point to the example brief. It shows what a signed-in user gets."
  • Keep the rest: keep the S50 sentences that are still true. Change "Change details and run again" to "Run again" wherever My Perch is described.

5. Limits

These are written for the README's Known limits. Each sentence is true of the code after this round's Tier A. The bullets under "Depends on Tier B" are dropped by the release session when that item shipped.

  • Accounts are not open on the test deploy, so visitors use guest mode, and the example brief shows what a signed-in user gets.
  • The example brief plays back a saved file, and it does not show cover-letter points.
  • Guests cannot paste a CV; the guest student path uses an invented sample student.
  • Each guest session has a small daily model budget, and when it is used the written reasons pause while the list, dates, amounts and rule results still show.
  • Perch folds only NIH activity codes P30, P01, P50 and U54 as centre and programme grants; other institution-level grants are listed with the single-lab grants.
  • The note to an office does not use the centre-grant label, and Scout reads the label but its wording is not tuned to it.
  • The Match number measures how closely a call's text matches the papers; it is not the odds of funding, and a card's written reason can be weaker than its Match band.
  • Several cards on one brief can cite the same papers.
  • Perch writes no reason for a Temple listing that gives only the award's name; the card points to the award's page instead.
  • The citation check can flag a correct sentence that joins two facts from one listing, and a flagged sentence is shown in a fold with a note.
  • Some cover-letter points can still be marked as not matched to their source.
  • Scout removes a sentence it cannot check, such as a claim that a record lacks a field, and marks the answer when it does.
  • Scout may mention that an account has added no CV or entries even when the question did not ask.
  • Asking for the same brief or the same cover-letter points again on the same day returns what was already built that day.
  • The Temple awards list sorts A to Z by default, so rows with no stated deadline or amount can come first.
  • The funding list still shows requests for information, which fund nothing; briefs leave them out.
  • Saves on the browse lists and keeps in a brief are two separate lists.
  • The note to an office waits for the model before any of it shows, which can take up to two minutes.
  • Run again sits in the brief's header and starts a new brief without asking first.
  • Only Grants.gov listings are refreshed on the deploy; other sources are as of their last fetch.

(Both Tier B items, H6 and H13, shipped in S51, so their bullets were dropped by the orchestrator after the re-check. The thin-listing order was fixed after the re-check too.)

S51 product, flow and demo review, round 3 of 3 (fresh context, 2026-11-05)docs/design/S51_PRODUCT_REVIEW.md, 5 Nov 2026

A read-only review of rebuild/v1 at b770886, the last round before release. It reads as three people: the presenter on stage, a guest in the audience on a phone, and a judge with the README. It also judges the real model text in build/s50_live/LIVE.md.

How to read this review:

  • Inputs: the code in web/ and perch/, the S50 walk screenshots in build/s50_qa_light/ and build/s50_qa_dark/, the deploy's example files in web/example/, the live capture build/s50_live/LIVE.md, and the round 2 documents.
  • Researchers: the live capture is PI-1 (A5063022331). The example brief is PI-4 (A5026494099). No other person is named here.
  • Walk screens use the fake model. Their model sentences are not real, so they are not filed. LIVE.md is the only real model text, and it is text, not screens.
  • Numbers: the deploy's spend ledger showed $1.26 of its $15 cap used at the time of this review. Guest limits are those in DECISIONS for 5 Nov: $4.00 an address and $8.00 a day. A researcher brief costs about $0.08, per RESULTS.

Must-fix before the demo

  • D1 Both example files are stale: web/example/researcher.json and student.json were built on 3 Nov, before S50. The researcher example has no Temple internal leads, because no lead carries group. Its one Scout answer is a single sentence from a local model, not the deploy's model. After rank 1, its matches read weak 30, 24, 14 and down to 3, which is a poor first look for a judge. The student example has no checks, so its cards fall back to the older verdict_lines. The example is what guests and judges are sent to from three places. Fix: re-export both from the final deploy after the S51 fixes. Pick a researcher whose brief has several good or strong matches, keep two individual-lab leads, draft the hand-off and ask two Scout questions before export. Keep the alias. Effort: small.
  • D2 Researcher cover points flag every line: in LIVE.md all five "You have" sentences on the top lead are marked unsupported. On screen that is five flagged lines and a warning box. The cause is not known yet. The test: read p.support in perch/skills/cover.py ground(). Scores of exactly 0.0 mean the cited papers were not found, which points to a key mismatch or an empty paper view. Small positive scores mean the claims are too compound, since each sentence joins two or three papers. Check also whether the cited 2025 and 2026 papers have abstracts in the store. Until it is fixed, the demo does not press cover points on a researcher card. Effort: small to diagnose.
  • D3 Centre and programme grants rank first: in LIVE.md the P30 Cancer Center Support Grant is rank 1 at "strong" 82. The P01, P50 and U54 calls sit at ranks 3, 7 and 8. A single lab cannot apply for these. The model says so in the text, but the pill still says strong, Scout repeats "strong match", and the hand-off asks Research Development about the P30. Fix in code: read the activity code from the title or record. For P30, P50, P01 and U54, add a code-written line, "An institution applies for this as a centre or programme, not a single lab." Sort these below individual awards such as R01, R21, R35 and K. No model and no new number is involved. Effort: small.
  • D4 The audience's first big button is a dead end: a first-time phone visitor sees "Browse Temple awards" and "Check my fit with my CV", in w360-landing.png. The second goes to sign-in, at web/app.js:410. Registration is off on the deploy, so nobody in the audience can get past it. The guest path is a small text link under it. Fix: while registration is off, the signed-out button reads "Try a sample student" and starts the guest session in one tap. The researcher side already starts a guest session on the first brief. Effort: small.
  • D5 Every "Sign in" wall leads nowhere for the audience: Scout, the hand-off and cover points show a primary "Sign in" button, at web/scout.js:88 and web/handoff.js:139. For Demo Day, make the example link the main action under each wall. Add one plain line: "Accounts are not open yet. See what a signed-in user gets in the example." Add the missing example link under the cover-points line. Effort: small.
  • D6 The student brief opens on its weakest cards: the audience's main path is "Try a sample student". In LIVE.md and w360-brief-student.png, the top three cards are name-only listings: Livingstone, Dean's Grant and the Pennsylvania State Grant. Each shows "Not stated" twice. Each model text opens "The record names X and gives no further detail", and MiniCheck flags that sentence. The 3 Nov example, also a SYNTHETIC undergraduate, led with NSF REU, Hollings, SROP and Truman, which fit an environmental-science junior far better. Fix two things. First, skip the model on a name-only listing and show a code-written line instead; this also saves spend. Second, find out why REU, Hollings and Truman left the top ten: check whether they are in the 30-lead pool and what S50's award_key merge or level rules did to them. Effort: small to medium.
  • D7 The presenter path has no run sheet and no pre-built briefs: round 2's Q38 was a run-sheet step, and nothing records that it was done. Build these on demo-presenter the morning of the demo: one researcher brief, done, with two individual-lab leads kept and the hand-off drafted. Ask one Scout question so the thread already holds an answer. Build one sample-student brief. Clear the guest spend and rate keys, as S52 task 2 says. Check that the spend ledger has at least $5 left. After signing in, use the app at least every 25 minutes, because the session ends after 30 idle minutes. Rehearse the fallback build once. Effort: small, no code.
  • D8 Ports may be blocked at the venue: the app is on port 8443 and sign-in is on port 10000. Many campus and venue networks allow only 443. Test from a phone on Temple Wi-Fi and on mobile data the day before. If 8443 fails, move the app to 443. The fallback build uses 443 today, so it then needs another port, or the swap must be reversible in a minute. Only the presenter needs the sign-in port, and the presenter can use a phone hotspot. Effort: small.
  • D9 Whose name goes on the projector, a decision for Dakshitha: a live researcher brief shows a real Temple researcher's name. Its hand-off is written in the first person, "My published work…", and signed with that name. Nothing in the repo records that this person agreed to appear on stage. Recommendation: present a researcher who has agreed, or present the aliased example for the researcher side. Do not search a stranger's name live. Effort: none, a decision.
  • D10 The README does not lead a judge to the example: the README never mentions the public deploy or "See an example brief". web/example/ is gitignored and left out of the package, so a judge who clones the repo and opens example.html sees "The example is not on this server." Fix: add one "See it" line near the top that links the deploy's example. Track the student example in the repo, because it holds only an invented student and public Temple listings. Keep the researcher example deploy-only. Effort: small.

Should-fix

  • D11 Scout volunteers what is missing: LIVE.md's second answer ends "You have not added a CV. You have no typed entries." Nobody asked. On stage it reads as a gap in the demo account. This is round 2's G14, absence tails, still not done. Fix: say what is missing only when the question is about the CV or entries. Giving demo-presenter a SYNTHETIC CV is the other option, but a fake CV beside a real researcher's papers mixes two people. Recommendation: fix the tail, add no CV. Effort: small.
  • D12 Scout's "closes soonest" answer has two shapes in one: it lists five leads without saying they are all leads, then switches to kept leads, then adds the P01. One heading sentence was withheld, so a "sentence removed" flag shows. Fix: when the question says "my leads", answer kept leads first. On stage, press the Deadlines chip instead, which code answers. Effort: small.
  • D13 Expiry shown as a deadline: the parent P01 card shows "Closes" with a 2029 date. Scout says the record has no deadline and that the date is when the announcement expires. Fix: when the date is the expiry of a parent announcement, label it "Announcement expires". Verify which record field holds it. Effort: small.
  • D14 "Your achievement A": student text names entries by a letter, as in "Your achievement A presented a poster…". Use the entry's own first words, or "One of your entries". Effort: small.
  • D15 Pill and text disagree: SHINE carries a "partial" pill at 50, while its text says "The fit is weak". The pill is code and the text is the model, so both are honest. A judge still sees a contradiction. D3 removes the worst case. For the rest, add one line in Help: "The match number ranks leads; the text says why." Effort: small.
  • D16 A spent guest budget is silent on the cards: when the guest budget runs out, the brief still finishes. The reason "withheld: the daily model budget is used" shows only inside Steps. The cards show no "Why it fits" and no reason. Fix: one line above the list that says the written reasons are paused for today and that the list, dates and amounts are unaffected. Effort: small.
  • D17 Canary tokens in the Load sample boxes: web/sample_student.js puts lines such as "Canary: PERCH-CANARY-UG-CV-3R8D" into the boxes the presenter fills on stage. Round 2's re-check filed this and it is still open. Fix: hide the canary line in the box and add it back on save. D7's pre-built brief avoids the screen for the demo. Effort: small.
  • D18 Old Temple calls in a researcher brief: LIVE.md lists the CIBER Research Award under Temple internal with a close date of 5 Dec 2022. Check what its card says. A call that closed almost four years ago should not appear in a list of routes. Also check the K01 mentored award from a Temple page, which is for early-career researchers. Effort: small.
  • D19 Industry ids are URLs: industry leads carry OpenAlex institution URLs as their record ids. The cards show the company name. Check the CSV and JSON exports and the compare table, and make sure none shows the URL as the title. Effort: small.
  • D20 Same three papers on most cards: in LIVE.md nine of ten grant cards cite the same three papers. A judge who opens two cards notices. Fix: when a card's papers match the card above, say "Draws on the same papers as above" and fold the list. Effort: small.
  • D21 The phone awards list opens on its weakest rows: "Temple awards" sorts A to Z by default, in w360-s50b-awards.png. The first screen shows "academic scholarships", "additional scholarships for sophomores…" and four "Not on the page" rows. Fix: default to rows with a stated deadline or amount first, then A to Z. Add round 2's "Has a deadline" filter if it is not already built. Effort: small.
  • D22 Small wording on student rule lines: "nothing there rules them out" is about one award, so it should be "rules it out". "Staff only: not listed as a staff or faculty award" reads like a restriction; say "Students: not a staff or faculty award." Effort: small.
  • D23 No real-model screens yet: LIVE.md is text. The demo will be the first time anyone sees the real text in the real layout, such as long fit text, a withheld line or a flag. Add a screenshot pass of the presenter path on the deploy to the rehearsal, as part of S52 task 7, and open every image. Effort: small.
  • D24 The README's numbers predate the demo settings: it says $0.10 a guest and $5.00 for all guests. The deploy now runs $4.00 an address and $8.00 a day. Name both, and say which one the demo uses. Effort: small.
  • D25 Run again sits next to Export: in the brief header, a mis-click on stage starts a new brief of about 40 seconds and new spend. Add a short confirm, or move Run again into the Steps panel. Effort: small.

Demo script

Five minutes, presenter on a laptop with the projector, audience on phones. Before it starts: D7's morning checks are done, D8's port test passed, and a QR code for the public URL is on the first slide.

  1. 0:00 Landing, in a private window: a signed-in window opens on My Perch, so keep two windows. The private window is signed out and shows what the audience sees. Show the tagline and the three promises in the footer. Say: "Scan the code, tap Student, then Try a sample student." Expected: the guest sample, once D4 is fixed. Fallback: say "Try it as a guest", the small link under the buttons.
  2. 0:30 Signed-in window, My Perch, then the researcher brief: open the pre-built researcher brief with one click. Expected: "Ready", the Grants tab, Match pills, D3's centre line on any P30 or P50. Fallback: open example.html.
  3. 1:00 One card, opened: open "Why it fits" on the top individual-lab lead, then press Evidence. Point out that the date and the amount in the panel are copied from the record. Expected: cited text and the evidence panel on the right. Fallback: the same card in the example.
  4. 1:40 Temple internal and Industry: one tap each. Check the Temple tab in the morning, and skip it if a closed call shows, as in D18. On an industry card, read the line "Inferred from public signals; not verified." Expected: two short lists. Fallback: skip; say the example has them.
  5. 2:10 Ask Scout: show the answer asked in the morning, then press the Deadlines chip live, which code answers at once. Do not type a new open question on stage. Expected: cited dates in seconds. Fallback: example.html?tab=scout.
  6. 2:50 Compare and hand-off: open Compare with the two kept leads. Scroll to the hand-off drafted in the morning. Point to the "Model text" label, the ERA line, and the words "Perch never sends it". Do not press "Open in my mail app" on the projector. Fallback: example.html?tab=compare.
  7. 3:40 Switch to Student: open the pre-built sample-student brief. Show the "Sample data" badge, a card with ✓ and ? rule lines, and on the Samples tab the card that fails on GPA, 3.50 asked and 3.40 on the CV. Find where that card sits in the morning, since not-eligible cards may be folded. Show cover points only if the morning run of one sample card came back with no flags. Fallback: example.html?side=student.
  8. 4:30 Close: "Every claim cites a public record. Nothing is sent. The audience is using it now." Put the QR code back up.
  • If sign-in fails: do steps 2 to 7 on the example pages. They need no sign-in and call no model.
  • If the deploy is down: run the fallback build, tag v0.1-demo-fallback, rehearsed once in D7.
  • If guests report empty reasons: that is D16, the guest budget. The lists, dates and rules still work. Say so and move on.
  • Slow steps to avoid live: a fresh researcher brief, about 38 to 50 seconds; cover points, up to two minutes; an open Scout question; Run again.

Leave for later

  • D26 One shortlist across Perch: merge browse saves and brief keeps, as round 2's Q34 said.
  • D27 Browse with fit for students: show rule verdicts on the awards list, as Q35 said.
  • D28 Code-only notes for guests: let guests get the code-written student note, as Q37 said. This needs Dakshitha's call after the demo.
  • D29 A graduate sample student: a second SYNTHETIC persona, as Q26 said.
  • D30 Delete one brief, untick a paper, agency filter and calendar file: Q27, Q28, Q29 and Q25.
  • D31 "[name removed]" inside quotes: award quotes on the awards list show the redaction marker twice in a sentence. Shorten the quote to start after the names.
  • D32 The hand-off waits for the model before showing the code parts: round 2's Q18. Pre-drafting in D7 hides it for the demo.
  • D33 A school read from the CV: the Dean's Grant card says "Perch does not know their school" for a student whose CV names a major. Map majors to schools later.

Judgement of the real model text in LIVE.md

  • Researcher text and the hand-off are useful and honest: each card says what the call funds, names cited papers and says where the fit is partial. The SHINE card says plainly that the work is malignant and the call is nonmalignant. The hand-off is the best output: fluent, with copied dates, links and papers. Its one problem is the P30, which D3 fixes. Cards run to about 80 to 110 words; D20 shortens them.
  • Scout and cover points read well but show as flawed: every Scout line is cited, but the tails in D11 and the mixed list in D12 read badly. The cover points pair "asks" and "you" clearly, but D2's flags make good text look wrong.
  • Student text is weakest where the listing is thin: on name-only listings the model has nothing to say and says so. D6 replaces that with a code line. On the sample scholarships the text is specific and correct.
S51 UI/UX review, round 3 of 3 (2026-11-05)docs/design/S51_UIUX_REVIEW.md, 5 Nov 2026

A fresh-context, read-only review of web/ on rebuild/v1, with the S50 full walk in build/s50_qa_light/ and build/s50_qa_dark/. Model text was judged against build/s50_live/LIVE.md, because the walk uses a fake model.

  • What was opened: every demo-path screen at both widths, a dark pass of the demo path, and contact sheets of the rest. Items fixed in round 2 or listed as closed in S50_RECHECK.md are not repeated.
  • Not bugs: a header drawn mid-page in the Scout, compare and hand-off captures is the sticky bar in a full-page screenshot.
  • Back-end items are marked "(back-end)" so the orchestrator can route them.
  • A suggested split for three builders: builder A takes the researcher brief and card (W2, W4 to W8, W13 to W15, W21 to W23). Builder B takes the student screens (W3, W9, W16 to W20). Builder C takes the shell, lists, Scout, hand-off and My Perch (W1, W10 to W12, W24 to W34).

Must-fix

  • W1. The example banner breaks on a phone: in w360-s50a-example, light and dark, the banner text is squeezed into a column about 150 px wide between the "Example" tag and "Back to Perch". It runs to eight lines. The row is .banner-line at web/styles.css:1386. Add @media (max-width: 599px) { .example-banner .banner-line { flex-wrap: wrap; } .example-banner .banner-line > span { flex-basis: 100%; order: 3; } }. The tag and the link then share the first row, and the text takes the full width under them.
  • W2. The example's "Brief ready" card is squeezed on a phone: in w360-s50a-example, "Built in 7 s · 8 of 8 steps" wraps one or two words per line. "Replay the build" and "Steps" take the rest of the row. The grid is .progress.compact at web/styles.css:265. Under 600 px, give the replay link and the Steps disclosure their own full-width row with grid-column: 1 / -1.
  • W3. Canary tokens still show after Load sample: w1280-s50c-find-after-sample and w360-s50c-find-after-sample show "Canary: PERCH-CANARY-UG-CV-3R8D" and the INT and ACH tokens in all three boxes. The text comes from web/sample_student.js:6, :32 and :35. Q17 decided that canaries are hidden on screen, and a presenter presses this button on stage. Fill the boxes with the noCanary text from web/student.js:57. On Save, put the canary line back when the text still starts with "SYNTHETIC example student (invented)", so the stored text keeps it, as rule 11 needs.
  • W4. A stopped brief still shows loading bars: w1280-s50a-stopped and w360-s50a-stopped show grey skeleton lines under "You stopped this brief". The code is at web/app.js:1702, where skeleton(3), skeleton(3) is drawn in every state. Draw the skeletons only while the brief is still building.
  • W5. "Run again" shows twice, and also during the build: w1280-s50a-stopped has a quiet "Run again" in the header and a primary "Run again" in the progress card. w1280-s50a-building shows "Run again" in the header next to Stop. Hide the header's Run again while the brief is queued or running, and while the stopped card shows its own button.
  • W6. The waiting text names a tab that does not exist: web/app.js:1702 says "The profile tab fills in first." The tab is called "What Perch read". Change the text to "What Perch read fills in first."
  • W7. Compare says "no explanation yet" on a finished brief (back-end): in w1280-handoff-ready and w360-handoff-ready every Evidence cell reads "no explanation yet". This comes from perch/compare.py:113. On a finished brief, or one with explanations turned off, write "no written reason" instead. The "Instrument or relationship" row at perch/compare.py:30 reads "Grant / funding instrument" on every grant, so it tells the reader nothing. Leave that row out when every column is a grant.
  • W8. One order has two names: the brief's sort says "Best match", but the compare sort says "Perch’s order" (web/compare.js:64). Both mean the Match score. Change the compare option to "Best match".
  • W9. The sample student brief mixes "the sample student" and "you": in w1280-cover-button, the header says "the sample student's CV", but the cover-letter line above the list says "A model writes these from your CV and entries." That line comes from coverListLine in web/cover.js:159-170. On a sample brief, say "the sample student's CV and entries", as cvWords() in web/student.js:64 does.
  • W10. The researcher landing's hint and disclosure do not line up: in w1280-s50a-landing-example-r, "Names search Temple authors; an ID finds anyone." sits about 10 px above "What else you can add". These are built at web/app.js:394-395. Give the row that holds them align-items: center, so the hint centres on the 44 px summary.
  • W11. The phone brief's filter chips take three rows: in w360-brief-researcher and w360-s50a-example, the chips All, NSF, NIH, then "DOE · Office of Science", R35 and RM1 wrap into three rows. That is about 150 px before the first card. The awards list already uses one row that scrolls sideways, which S50 decided. Use the same rule for the brief's chip row under 600 px.
  • W12. Actions jump between My Perch brief rows: in w1280-s49b-my-perch, "Open" sits at x≈488 on one row and x≈391 on the busy row, because Stop is placed in between. Keep a fixed order: Open, then Run again, then Stop last. The link at web/account.js:351 also says "Change details and run again", while the brief header says "Run again". Use "Run again" as the visible text, with the long phrase as its aria-label, as web/app.js:926 already does.

Polish (ranked by impact)

  • W13. Put the fit verdict on the researcher card's face (top item): the visible part of a researcher card is "what the call funds" (explanationBlock, web/app.js:2112). In LIVE this is about 60 words restating the call. The useful sentence is the inference, such as "The fit is weak, because these papers center on … malignant blood disorders". That sentence sits inside a closed "Why it fits" disclosure. The student card already leads with it (fitReason, web/student.js:498). Render a p.fit-why with a bold "Why it fits:" or "How it relates:", the inference through renderSegs, and the Model text tag, right under the facts. Move the "what it funds" sentence into the disclosure, above the findings.
  • W14. Keep five real explanations from filling the screen: LIVE explanations run 80 to 110 words, with three findings and an inference each. With a CV in the brief, every card starts open (web/app.js:2121), so the first five cards are very tall. Start only the first card open. Clamp .explain .what to three lines with -webkit-line-clamp: 3, and let the disclosure show the rest.
  • W15. Lighten the card footer: in w1280-brief-researcher, the footer with outlined Keep and Dismiss and a rule line is about a third of each card's height. It repeats ten times. Make Dismiss btn quiet, with no border, and keep Keep outlined. Drop the top rule when the footer holds no cover block: .lead-foot:not(:has(.cover)) { border-top: 0; padding-top: 4px; }. Both buttons keep their 44 px height.
  • W16. The student card says "no deadline" twice: in w1280-brief-student, the Livingstone and PASG cards show "Deadline: Not stated" in the facts and "? Deadline: the listing gives no date." in the rule lines. In rulesBlock (web/student.js:40), leave out an unknown check for the deadline rule when the card has no deadline in its facts. Check the rule's id in perch/student.py first.
  • W17. Temple-page awards show "Not stated" twice: the top three student cards in w1280-brief-student read "Not stated / Not stated". Extend the G7 one-line fact (neither, web/student.js:463) to temple_pages records: "The page gives neither. Check the award’s own page." The Boren line is drawn in bold ink, while "Not stated" is muted. Give .fact-wide dd regular weight so the two read alike.
  • W18. Leave passed rules out of "Every option below": the shared note in w1280-brief-student lists "Staff only: not listed as a staff or faculty award." A judge reads this as a warning. Show only unknown and fail lines in the note. Passed lines that every card shares can move into "About this list".
  • W19. Soften the unsupported-sentence box: web/student.js:487 and the researcher card use the amber warn notice. In LIVE, all of the top three student cards carry an unsupported sentence. An amber box on every card reads as broken. Use a quiet details with the summary "1 sentence could not be matched to its source", opening to the list. It is just as honest and less alarming. This matters less if the back-end skips the model for thin listings, as the orchestrator notes suggest.
  • W20. Entry labels read badly: plainExplanation (web/student.js:529) turns an id into "your achievement A", so LIVE reads "Your achievement A presented a poster …". Use the entry's first five words, as the Read tab already does (web/student.js:298-299), or "One of your entries".
  • W21. "Weaker matches" follows cards that are already weak: the open list shows "Match weak 23", "15" and "14", then a fold named "Weaker matches (5)" (web/app.js:1771). The fold only holds cards after the first five (OPEN_FIRST, :1814). Rename it "Show 5 more".
  • W22. Say once what the Match number is: the pill "Match good 67" has no visible scale. The screen-reader text at web/student.js:416 already says "out of 100 … not the odds of funding". Show one hint line in the list head: "Match: how closely the call’s text matches the papers, out of 100. It is not the odds of funding."
  • W23. Name the hand-off where people look for it: the shortlist button says "Compare and draft", but the tab says "Compare (2)", and the hand-off lives under that tab. At 600 px and wider, name the tab "Compare and draft (2)". The phone keeps "Compare".
  • W24. Use one link style per role: there are three styles. Green bold underline is used for "Try it as a guest" and "Sign in". Grey bold .quiet-link (web/styles.css:1397) is used for "See an example brief" and "Manage in Account and data". Green regular is used for "Find your research administrator". In w1280-handoff-ready, two links in neighbouring lines differ in weight. Use one rule: links inside a sentence are moss at weight 500, and standalone links are .quiet-link. This was V46, deferred from round 2.
  • W25. One label for the example link: web/app.js:451 says "See an example" on the student side and "See an example brief" on the researcher side. Use "See an example brief" on both.
  • W26. Scout's "Local model" caption is jargon to a judge: the centred caption under each answer comes from web/scout.js:263 and :268. Use a short sentence that says what it means on the deploy, such as "Written by the model on Perch’s own server". The orchestrator should confirm the wording is true for the deploy before it ships.
  • W27. Align Scout's guest wall with its chat column: the guest wall in w1280-brief-researcher-scout sits flush left. The chat in w1280-scout-clean is a centred column about 870 px wide. Put the wall in the same centred column. "New conversation" is a filled grey chip, unlike every other secondary button. Make it btn.
  • W28. The hand-off wait looks frozen: web/handoff.js:113 shows one hint line, "This can take up to two minutes…", and nothing moves (w360-handoff-busy). Add the owl's "work" pose and two skeleton() lines where the draft will appear, as a card does while it is "Reading".
  • W29. My Perch's empty state repeats its buttons: in w1280-my-perch, "Browse Temple awards" and "Check my fit" sit in the page head and again inside each empty card. Drop the in-card buttons when the head has them. The small owl sits flush left above the empty line; centre the owl and the line, or leave the owl out.
  • W30. My Perch's title is tight under the bar: in w1280-my-perch, the h1 starts about 20 px under the app bar. Brief pages have Back and about 40 px. Add padding-top: 24px to the My Perch head.
  • W31. Industry cards repeat the list banner: each card in w1280-s50a-industry shows "Inference · Inferred from public signals; not verified." This is the fallback in orgCard (web/app.js:1965), and the banner above the list says the same. Show the line only when l.inference has the model's own sentence.
  • W32. Facts come in a different order on the funding list: browse rows show Amount, then Closes (w1280-funding). Cards show Closes, then Amount. Use Closes first everywhere. Add the relative date, such as "in 3 days", from f.closesIn on browse rows as cards do. The list sorts by "Closing soonest", and today's rows give no sign that they close today.
  • W33. "Award horizon" reads as an error: in w1280-s50a-threads, "30 Jun 2016 · already passed" is the largest text on What Perch read. Set it at section-title size. Label it "Last federal award ended 30 Jun 2016" (web/app.js:1491-1503).
  • W34. The thread subtitle is a fragment: "of the weight, recent papers counting more" (web/app.js:1598) hangs under "Thread 1 · 73 %". Write "73 % of the papers’ weight. Newer papers count more."

Leave for later

  • W35. A summary line on the Routes tab: the researcher's one-line summary lives only on What Perch read. A cited teaser above the routes would help a judge, but it needs model-text handling on a new spot.
  • W36. Requests for information on the funding list: DE-FOA-0003671 shows "$1 to $2" in w1280-funding. Q9 was deferred. The cheap version is a "Request for information" tag on the row.
  • W37. Two back links on the pick screen: w360-s50a-pick has "Back to the matches" and "Choose someone else" stacked. Merge them into one.
  • W38. Empty space on the landing at 1280 x 860: about 220 px sits blank above the footer in w1280-landing-guest. A three-step strip could fill it, but the page already works.
  • W39. Student compare wording: the compare says "Not stated in the record", while the cards say "Not stated". Unify it with the shared compare table (V11).
S50 design: round 2 build spec (2026-11-05)docs/design/S50_DESIGN.md, 5 Nov 2026

This spec turns the four round 2 reviews into one front-end build. Round 3 follows it, then the release. It reuses the S49 conventions: the walk-flow loader, the package rules in S49_DESIGN.md section 3.1, and the shared-contract style ("A styles it; A and C emit it").

Item codes refer to these documents:

  • V1 to V51: S50_UIUX_REVIEW.md.
  • Q1 to Q38: S50_PRODUCT_REVIEW.md.
  • G1 to G34: S50_FUNCTION_REVIEW.md. Only G7, G8 and G19 are front-end work.
  • C1 to C30: S50_BACKEND_REVIEW.md. Only C3 reaches the screen.
  • LIVE: the real-model capture in build/s50_live/LIVE.md.

The walk researcher is PI-4 (A5026494099). The example brief uses the aliased replay of PI-4. No other researcher is named here.

1. Decisions

The orchestrator settles these. Each one goes into docs/DECISIONS.md when the spec is recorded.

  • Keep and Dismiss move to a footer row (V2, V39, Q16): the title row keeps only the Match pill. So the title gets about 650 px of an 840 px card, not 310 to 450 px.
  • The footer row also holds the Cover-letter points button, on its left: a card then has one row of actions, not two. When points arrive, they open full width under the footer row.
  • The student verdict chip moves into the rule block (V4, Q1): the chip sits on top of the lines that explain it. "To check:" and "Why not:" labels go away.
  • Rule lines come from lead.checks (P6, Q1, G6): code writes each line, and the UI shows the text as it came. When the field is missing, the card falls back to verdict_lines.
  • A line that every card repeats is said once (V4, V5, decided): when three or more cards on a list share one rule line, the line moves above the list as "Every option below: <line>". Each card then drops it.
  • The withheld-reason line is said once (V5): when the list note about failed citation checks shows, the cards show no withheld line. A card with no reason section is the withheld one, and the list note says so.
  • The cover-letter hint is said once (V5): a signed-in user sees one line above the list. Cards show only the button.
  • Facts sit in a fixed grid (V6): two columns of 220 px, so Closes and Amount line up down the list.
  • One Match pill shape (V41): the shape is the same in every band. Only the tint changes: filled green for strong, soft green for good, grey for partial and weak.
  • Sort becomes a small select (V3, V42): the options are "Best match" and "Closing soonest". "Best match" sorts by match_score, highest first, with the server's rank as the tie-break. This fixes the out-of-order route T list.
  • The example brief is a static replay page (Q22, decided): web/example.html loads web/example/<side>.json and plays it in the app's existing replay mode. The JSON is gitignored and placed on the deploy. It needs no server code and no model call, and it cannot stall.
  • The example is labelled plainly: a banner says "Example", names the researcher by alias, gives the build date and says it plays back from a file. The landing link shows only when the file is on the server.
  • Guests get one "Or see an example" link under two walls (Q7 slice): the links sit under "Sign in to ask Scout" and under "Sign in to draft a note to the office". Each one opens that tab of the example brief. The cover-points wall is already one line above the list, so it gets no link.
  • Phone filters fold (V9, V40, Q14, decided): under 600 px, the search box stays and one "Filters" button opens the rest. School chips become one row that scrolls sideways.
  • Controls get a 3:1 border (V10, decided): a new token --line-strong is #7E8B85 in light mode and #687B74 in dark mode. It is 3.1:1 or more against the page, cards and chips in both themes. Fields, secondary buttons, the ready chip and the sort select use it. Card edges keep --line.
  • Disabled buttons look disabled (V27): a disabled button gets the chip fill, the faint border and muted text, with no opacity trick.
  • Focus on a heading moved by code shows no ring (V1, decided): the rule covers h1, h2 and h3 with tabindex="-1". Keyboard focus on every control keeps the ring.
  • Stop is for signed-in users only (Q6): the cancel route refuses guests, so a guest never sees a Stop button.
  • Far-off dates on the funding list use the card's rule (G8): a date more than ten years out with a note shows the note. The server's G8 fix replaces the rest.
  • Page words on the funding list are quoted (V29): a record with no date and with its own words shows "The page says: “…”", as the awards list does.
  • "Not on the page" in the awards column (Q21): the narrow column says this. The full sentence stays in the evidence panel.
  • Temple internal calls leave the Research Development note (Q3): handoff.js counts only federal grants for that office. A line under the office choice says where Temple's own calls send people.
  • Student list heading (Q8): it reads "N awards to look into". It no longer claims "you may apply for".
  • Canary tokens are hidden on screen only (Q17): stored text, exports and the leak checks keep them, as rule 11 needs.
  • Lower-case Temple titles stay as written (Q20): the round 1 decision stands, because a title is copied record text.
  • The researcher's name on My Perch rows waits (Q12): /me/briefs has no display name. The row gets the time instead, and the name needs a back-end field later.

For Dakshitha

  • None. Q20 is the only real fork. It was settled in round 1 (keep the record's text), and this spec keeps that. If Dakshitha wants it reopened, it is one CSS rule in round 3.

2. Scope for round 2

The budget is about 4 to 5 hours of builder time, run by 3 builders in parallel. Each package lists its items in build order with minute estimates. Tier A must ship. Tier B ships only if the package is under budget, cut from the bottom first.

  • Tier A adds up to about 325 minutes: FE-A is about 115, FE-B about 120 and FE-C about 90. That is about 5.4 hours, a little over the target. The decided items and the review must-fixes alone need about 4.5 hours.
  • Tier B adds about 150 minutes more. It is polish that round 3 can take if this round runs short.
  • The cut line, if the orchestrator holds to 4.5 hours: move these to round 3, in this order.
    • FE-B B1's V7 search button: keep the doubled border for one more round. This saves 10 minutes.
    • FE-C C4's merged facts line for fellowships-list records (G7): the cards keep "Not stated". This saves 10 minutes.
    • FE-A A6's "Hidden" disclosure (V44): keep the run-on line. This saves 8 minutes.
    • FE-B B3's hand-off error placement (V24): keep the wording fix only. This saves 5 minutes.

Must-fix coverage

Every must-fix item that is front-end work is in Tier A:

  • UI/UX review: V1 is A1. V2 is A2 and C1. V3 is A3. V4 is C2. V5 is B4, A2 and C2. V6 is A2. V7 is B1. V8 is A1. V9 is B1. V10 is A1.
  • Product review:
    • Q1 is C2 and C5.
    • Q3 is B3.
    • Q4 is C3.
    • Q6 is A4 and B2.
    • Q7, as the two example links, is B3 and B5.
    • Q22 is A5.
    • Q2 is back-end data work. Q5 is done: the live capture is build/s50_live/LIVE.md.
  • Function review: G7 is C4. G8 is B1. G19 is C4. G1 to G6 are back-end work.
  • Back-end review: C3 is shown by B2. The status field comes from the back-end package.

Deferred to round 3 or later, with reasons

  • V11 (two Compare screens): this round gives both the same heading and note order (C5). One shared table component is a larger refactor across two owners.
  • V15 (steps text): the text is written in perch/service.py, which the back-end package owns. It is passed to the back-end builder as a one-line note.
  • V23 (cover actions in one row): the change is small, but it touches scout.js and cover.js together. It goes in round 3 with V49.
  • V25 and Q18 (hand-off wait shows the draft frame): the product review dates this after Demo Day, and it needs a server split of the draft.
  • V46, V49, V50 (link styles, Scout column, separator dots): polish only, so round 3.
  • Q9 (request for information on funding): the back-end G3 rule hides these from briefs. A browse tag is FE-B Tier B.
  • Q12 researcher name: it needs a back-end field, as noted above.
  • Q23 (has-a-deadline filters): the lists are paged on the server, so this needs new query parameters.
  • Q24 to Q29 and Q34 to Q38: the product review dates them after Demo Day. Q38 is a run-sheet step, not code.
  • Q37: a fork for Dakshitha after Demo Day. The account rule stands for the demo.
  • LIVE, industry titles: the capture showed OpenAlex institution URLs where the organisation name was missing in the payload. orgCard already falls back to record_id. QA checks the screen in round 3. A fix belongs in the payload, not the UI.
  • LIVE, raw ids in student prose: fitReason already strips a leading user:achievement-x. QA checks one real student card in round 3.

3. Build packages

3.0 Step 0, done by the orchestrator before any builder starts (about 15 minutes, one commit)

These changes let three worktrees build without touching each other's files.

  • web/api.js, two methods on the live API:
    • cancelBrief(id): post(${bid(id)}/cancel). It returns {"id": "<id>", "cancelled": true|false} and a 404 for a guest.
    • exampleAvailable(side): a HEAD fetch of example/${side}.json, kept in a module-level map so it runs once per side. It resolves to true or false and never throws.
  • web/api.js, the replay API: cancelBrief rejects with new ApiError("Stopping needs the live app.", 0). exampleAvailable resolves to false.
  • web/dom.js: add info: "M12 21a9 9 0 1 0 0-18 9 9 0 0 0 0 18zM12 11v5M12 8h.01" to the icon paths.
  • .gitignore: add web/example/.
  • Walk flow files: create scripts/walk_flows/s50_fe_a.py, s50_fe_b.py and s50_fe_c.py. Each holds def register(U): return {}, [].
  • Example files on the deploy checkout:
    • Copy build/replay/MCp4CdcfZLK8.json (PI-4, saved 3 Nov 2026, with compare, hand-offs and Scout) to web/example/researcher.json.
    • Copy build/replay/student.json (the SYNTHETIC student preview) to web/example/student.json.
    • Before copying, open each file and check five things. The researcher shows as "PI-4" only. The created date is right. compare, handoffs and scout are there. The recorded hand-off lead ids are the leads marked kept in the file. No explanation or inference field in the researcher file contains "SYNTHETIC": the walk's fake model writes that word, so a hit means the file came from a walk, not from real models, and it must not be used.
    • If a fresh researcher replay can be exported from the v1 deploy store, prefer it.
    • These files are gitignored, so they never enter the repo or the ZIP. The v1 test deploy runs from this checkout, so it serves them at once.
  • Walk server: start it with PERCH_SCHEDULER=0, so the nightly precache never runs during a walk (C2, C19).
  • Who owns which flow file:
    • FE-A owns s50_fe_a.py and the old s49_fe_a.py.
    • FE-B owns s50_fe_b.py and the old s49_fe_b.py.
    • FE-C owns s50_fe_c.py and the old s49_be_s.py.

3.1 Rules for every package

The S49 rules apply unchanged (S49_DESIGN.md section 3.1). They cover isolation, fail first, one walk server on port 8191 started through scripts/run_limited.sh, existing checks, tests, final copy, commits and escalation. Four additions:

  • Worktrees lack the example files: web/example/ is gitignored, so a worktree does not have it. A walk check stubs **/example/*.json with Playwright's page.route. It serves the cached PI-4 payload that s49_fe_a.py already keeps under build/s49_fe_a/cache, wrapped as a replay file: {"version": 2, "brief": <payload>, "candidates": [{"display_name": "PI-4"}], "records": {}}.
  • Old checks in ux_walk.py that this round breaks on purpose: the builder lists them in the hand-back, and the orchestrator edits ux_walk.py after the merge. These are known now:
    • cover_student_hint and cover_researcher_hint (lines 906 and 1023): the hint moves above the list.
    • cover_hint_hidden_with_result (line 941).
    • The [data-key=sort-closing] click (line 989): Sort is now a select.
  • Old checks in scripts/walk_flows/s49_*.py: each owner updates its own. Examples are CARDS (titleTop and actTop) and CENTRES (the sort group) in s49_fe_a.py, and the withheld-line count in s49_be_s.py.
  • Contracts that may be missing: the back-end fields this round reads (lead.checks, the C3 status, the G8 words) may not be merged yet. Every screen must work without them, and the walk stubs them with SYNTHETIC values.

Rule block (FE-C emits it; FE-A styles it)
div.rules[data-verdict="eligible"|"may"|"not"]
  verdictChip(l.verdict)                       the existing span.verdict
  ul.checks
    li.check[data-outcome="fail"|"unknown"|"pass"]
      span.check-mk[aria-hidden=true]          "✕" | "?" | "✓"
      span.sr-only                             "Not met: " | "Not known: " | "Met: "
      span                                     the line's text, verbatim

    summary                                    "N more checks"
    ul.checks > li.check ...
  • The source, when l.checks is an array: one li per item. The order is fail, then unknown, then pass, keeping the server's order inside each group. The text is rendered exactly as it came. The UI never reformats a number or a date in it.
  • The source, when l.checks is missing: one li per verdict_lines item. Its outcome is fail when the verdict is "not eligible" and unknown otherwise. The one exception is the eligible line "Meets every rule Perch checks.", which is pass.
  • Lines already said above the list (see below) are left out of the card.
  • An empty block: when no line is left, the block holds the chip alone.

div.list-head

  • The shared-rule note's text: "Every option below: <line>". It uses icon("info").

Example page (FE-A builds it; FE-B links to it)

A5. The example brief (Q22) (30 minutes)
  • web/example.html: a copy of index.html with three differences.
    • The title: <title>Example brief — Perch</title>.
    • The wordmark: href="./".
    • The script: <script type="module" src="example.js"></script> in place of app.js.
  • web/example.js:
  // The example brief (S50 Q22): a saved brief played back in the app's replay mode, from a file the
  // deploy places at web/example/<side>.json. Nothing is called and nothing is saved.
  const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  const side = q.get("side") === "student" ? "student" : "researcher";
  const tab = ["routes", "profile", "compare", "scout"].includes(q.get("tab")) ? q.get("tab") : "routes";
  try {
    const r = await fetch(`example/${side}.json`, { cache: "no-cache" });
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(String(r.status));
    const data = await r.json();
    window.PERCH_REPLAY = data;
    window.PERCH_EXAMPLE = { side };
    if (!location.hash || location.hash === "#/") {
      history.replaceState(null, "", `#/brief/${encodeURIComponent(data.brief.brief.id)}/${tab}`);
    }
    await import("./app.js");
  } catch {
    // draw into <main>: h1 "The example is not on this server.", then a link "Back to Perch" to "./"
  }
  • The CSP stays as it is: script-src 'self' allows both files, and the JSON is fetched under connect-src 'self'. The inline-script page that build_ui_preview.py makes would be blocked here, so it is not used.

Every sentence below must be true of the merged code. FE-B checks each one against the code before it closes B6.

  • The lead card (update the anatomy figure and its callouts): "The title comes first, with the Match pill beside it. Closes and Amount sit in two columns. Keep, Dismiss and Cover-letter points sit in the card's bottom row."

A check mark means the rule was met, a cross means it was not, and a question mark means the listing or your CV does not say. When every card shares a line, it is said once above the list."

S50 UI/UX review, round 2 of 3 (2026-11-05)docs/design/S50_UIUX_REVIEW.md, 5 Nov 2026

A fresh-context review of the front end on rebuild/v1. It is read-only; this file is the only edit.

  • Inputs: the code in web/ and the screenshots in build/s49_qa_light/ and build/s49_qa_dark/.
  • Desktop coverage: every 1280 px light state was opened at full size. Dark 1280 px states were opened full size where they differ, and as contact sheets for the rest.
  • Phone coverage: 20 phone states were opened at full size, light and dark side by side. They are the landing, both briefs, the student list, awards, awards empty, funding, the funding error, My Perch, both compares, welcome, account, the steps chip, Scout, the hand-off draft and error, the cover result and quota, the pick screen, the researcher profile, and the delete and withdraw dialogs. The other phone states were not opened one by one.
  • Screenshot vintage: the walk ran at commit 115fdb6. The only later change to web/ is 11f12bf, which changes the no-worker waiting text in web/app.js. No screenshot is stale for this review.
  • Round 1 context: items already closed in S49_RECHECK.md are not listed again. Leftovers that are still visible are listed and marked "leftover". Items that round 1 made worse are marked "made worse in round 1".
  • Researcher naming: the walk researcher is PI-4, A5026494099. No real name appears here.
  • Contrast was measured, not guessed: body text pairs all pass 4.5:1. The muted ink on the page is 5.4:1. The eligibility pill is 6.6:1. Dark muted ink is 6.9:1. The failures are listed under V10 and V27.
  • Not reviewed, because there is no screenshot: the Help page, the researcher matches list before a pick, a brief while it builds, the evidence rail with a record open, the Industry route list, the student sample route list, and "Weaker matches" when it is open.
  • Not defects: in the Scout and hand-off screenshots the site header appears halfway down the page. This is how a full-page capture draws a sticky header and the sticky tabs. It is not a layout bug.

Must-fix

  • V1 Heading focus box, leftover: after each route change, the page heading shows a full-width blue box. It shows on awards, funding, samples, welcome and the student start, in both themes. The cause is the global :focus-visible rule hitting headings that code focuses. A scoped rule such as h1[tabindex="-1"]:focus { outline: none; } fixes it and keeps the screen-reader move. Code: web/styles.css:94, web/account.js:62, web/browse.js:335, web/browse.js:402, web/student.js:140. Screenshots: w1280-awards, w1280-welcome, w1280-s49b-welcome, w360-awards, dark w1280-samples.
  • V2 Card titles squeezed, made worse in round 1: the card head is a two-column grid. The right column holds the match pill, the eligibility pill and two buttons, and it never wraps. So the title column is about 450 px wide on researcher cards and about 310 px on student cards, in a card that is 840 px wide. Short titles such as "SYNTHETIC Harbor Prize" break over two lines. Move Keep and Dismiss to a footer row of the card, or put the pills under the title. Code: web/styles.css:1506, web/styles.css:1508, web/app.js:1842, web/app.js:1961, web/student.js:387. Screenshots: w1280-s49-student-list, w1280-brief-student, w1280-brief-researcher.
  • V3 "Score" sort is out of order on Temple internal: the button says Score, but the code sorts by the server's rank. On route T the Match numbers read 6, 55, 2, 45, 44 from top to bottom. Those two cards are planted SYNTHETIC records, and the Grants route is in order, so real data may hide this. The label still promises an order the code does not give. Sort by match_score when the label says Score, or rename the button "Perch's order", as the phone compare already does. Code: web/app.js:1529-1535, web/app.js:1557. Screenshot: w1280-s49a-route-t.
  • V4 The same "To check" line on every student card, leftover P6: all ten cards on the sample brief say "The listing says who may apply; the award's own page sets the full rules." It tells the student nothing and makes the cards look copied. Show a code-written line that says what the rules checked. If that is not ready, show the sentence once above the list. Code: web/student.js:393. Screenshot: w1280-brief-student.
  • V5 Hints repeated on every card, made worse in round 1: two sentences now repeat on every card of one list. One is "A model writes these from your CV and entries. You put them in your own words." under each Cover-letter points button. The other is "Written reason withheld: it failed the citation check." under a notice that already says so. Show each one once above the list, as the guest line already does. Code: web/cover.js:10-11, web/cover.js:179, web/app.js:1687, web/app.js:1924, web/student.js:399. Screenshots: w1280-s49-student-list, w1280-s49-student-list-clean, dark w1280-brief-researcher.
  • V6 Fact columns jump between cards, made worse in round 1: Closes and Amount sit in a wrapping flex row. So the Amount column starts at three different places in one list: 106 px, 223 px and 239 px from the card's inner edge. Use a grid with two fixed columns, about 220 px each, so the facts line up down the list. Code: web/styles.css:1515. Screenshots: w1280-brief-researcher, w1280-s49a-route-t, w1280-s49-student-list.
  • V7 Search button doubled border, leftover: the Search button sits inside the bordered search box. That gives two borders side by side. On a phone it becomes a full-width button inside the box. Put the button outside the box, or drop the outer border and give the input its own border. The clear "×" inside the box is also the browser's own blue; style it with the ink colour. Code: web/styles.css:957-961, web/styles.css:1179-1180, web/browse.js:313-316. Screenshots: w1280-awards, w1280-awards-empty, w360-awards, w360-s49b-funding.
  • V8 Form column off-centre, made worse in round 1: the form screen is 760 px wide, but its cards and buttons are capped at 680 px and sit on the left. On welcome and account the cards sit 40 px left of centre, with 80 px of empty column on their right. On the student start the cards are 760 px and the "Find awards that fit" button is 680 px, so the two right edges do not line up. Use one width for the whole column. Code: web/pages.css:103, web/styles.css:1425, web/styles.css:1428. Screenshots: w1280-welcome, w1280-account, w1280-student-start.
  • V9 Phone lists start two screens down: on a phone, the awards list shows 17 school chips in about ten rows. The funding list stacks search, two selects, two switches and a hint. The first record appears after 700 to 1100 px of controls. Make the chip row one line that scrolls sideways on a phone. Fold level, sort and the switches into one "Filters" button. Code: web/styles.css:1526, web/browse.js:304-328. Screenshots: w360-awards, w360-s49b-awards-signed, w360-s49b-funding.
  • V10 Field and button borders too faint: the border token is 1.22:1 against the page in light mode and 1.29:1 against a card in dark mode. WCAG 1.4.11 asks for 3:1 when the border is what shows a field or button. The search box and the secondary buttons rely on that border, and in dark mode "Check my fit with my CV" almost disappears. Add a stronger border token for inputs and secondary buttons, and keep the faint one for card edges. Code: web/styles.css:24, web/styles.css:53, web/styles.css:68. The student compare has plain headers, tight rows, its note at the bottom and the heading "Draft a note to a Temple office". The researcher table also indents its "Lead" header 12 px past the cells under it. Build both from one table and one hand-off block.
