S50 product and flow review, round 2 of 3 (fresh context, 2026-11-05)docs/design/S50_PRODUCT_REVIEW.md, 5 Nov 2026

Read-only review of the v1 web app on rebuild/v1 at 61dfebd. Inputs: the S49 QA screenshots in build/s49_qa_light/ and build/s49_qa_dark/, the code in web/, the routes in perch/api.py, perch/browse/routes.py and perch/user/, and the round 1 documents S49_PRODUCT_REVIEW.md, S49_DESIGN.md, S49_RECHECK.md and S49_ORCHESTRATOR_NOTES.md.

How to read this review:

  • Fake model: the walk ran the fake model on a seeded store. Explanation text, scores and the order of cards are not real, so they are not filed as bugs. Verdict chips and their lines are written by code, so they are real.
  • Five readers: an undergraduate, a graduate student, a faculty researcher, a Demo Day judge with three minutes, and the presenter, who is signed in as a SYNTHETIC account while the audience uses guest mode.
  • Timing: the gate is today at 6:00 pm and Demo Day is tomorrow. Each item says "before the gate" or "after Demo Day".
  • Researcher: the walk researcher is PI-4, OpenAlex A5026494099. No other person is named.

Must-fix

  • Q1 Every student card says the same thing, P6 still open: All ten cards in w1280-s49a-brief-student.png carry the same "To check" sentence. It comes from the listing_only branch at perch/student.py:296-300. Add checked: list[str] to Verdict at perch/student.py:138-144. Fill it in check() with one code-written line per rule that ran and passed, such as "Level: open to undergraduates; your CV says bachelor's." Add a line for each rule that could not run, such as "Level: the listing does not state one." Show both on the card and in the "Rule check" column of the student compare. Effort: small to medium. When: before the gate.
  • Q2 Postdoctoral fellowships pass a junior's rules: The sample student is a year-3 bachelor's student. The top two cards are "NRSA Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship (F32)" and "Senior Postdoctoral Fellowship (F33)", both "May be eligible", in w360-s49a-brief-student.png. The NIH path already rules F32 out at perch/student.py:336-339. The Temple fellowships-office copy of the same award has no level, so study_levels at perch/student.py:201-204 returns nothing and no level rule runs. Set the audience level to postdoc for these listings in data/overrides/, so student_pool at perch/student.py:439 leaves them out. Check the live deploy first, because the walk store is seeded. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q3 Kept Temple internal calls go to the wrong office: Temple internal leads are stored with route="A" at perch/service.py:454. The hand-off picks kept leads by route only, at perch/service.py:211-212, and web/handoff.js:78 counts them the same way. So a kept internal call is counted as a "kept grant" and drafted to Research Development. Compare says the opposite, "Named on the call's page", at perch/compare.py:128-131. Leave group == "temple_internal" leads out of the office draft. Add one code-written line under the radio instead: "Temple's own calls name their contact on each call's page." Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q4 Load sample then three separate saves: After "Load sample", "Find awards that fit" stays disabled with "Save your CV first", in w1280-s49-load-sample-after.png. The presenter must press Save my CV, Save interests and Add achievement, then Find. That is four presses on stage for one action. Make "Find awards that fit" save every filled, unsaved box first, then build. Keep the separate buttons for editing. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q5 No one has reviewed a real brief yet: Round 1 asked for one live capture as S15, and round 2 still has none. Every model sentence in the screenshots is fake. Capture one researcher brief for PI-4 and one sample-student brief on the test deploy with scripts/smoke_deploy.py. Save the screens for round 3. Check the fit text, cover points, one Scout answer and one hand-off draft. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q6 A stuck brief has no way out: My Perch shows a brief that is "Still building" in w1280-s49b-my-perch.png. That row may be a walk stub, but the gap is real. A cancel route exists at perch/api.py:877, but nothing in web/ calls it. Add a "Stop" button on a busy row and on the brief's waiting screen. A stopped brief then shows "Stopped" and can be run again. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q7 Guests hit three sign-in walls on the demo path: A guest sees "Sign in to ask Scout" in w1280-scout-guest.png, "Sign in to draft a note to the office" in w1280-brief-researcher-compare.png, and a sign-in line instead of cover-letter points. These are three of the four things the presenter will show. The account rule stays as decided on 2026-11-04. Under each wall, add a small, static, SYNTHETIC example of the finished result, labelled "Example". Build it from the replay page that scripts/export_replay.py already makes. Effort: medium. When: before the gate.

Should-fix

  • Q8 "Options you may apply for" claims too much: The list head reads "10 options you may apply for" while every chip says "May be eligible", in w1280-s49a-brief-student.png. When no card is "eligible", say "10 awards to look into". Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q9 A request for information shows as funding: The funding list shows "Request for Information - Gauging Investor Interest" with an amount of "$1 to $2", in w1280-s49b-funding.png. This is not a call that pays. Tag records whose title starts "Request for Information" as "Request for information: not a funding call". The tag is code reading the record's own title. Leave them out of researcher briefs. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q10 The funding list does not say how soon a call closes: Brief cards say "in 11 months", but list rows show only the date. The first rows close today, in w1280-s49b-funding.png. Add the same relative text, and the amber style used for "in 13 days" in w1280-s49a-route-t.png. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q11 A saved award is a dead end: On My Perch a saved row offers only Evidence and Remove, in w1280-s49b-my-perch.png. Add the external link to the award's page, as the browse row has. Make "Kept in your brief of 3 Nov 2026" a link to that brief. The code is keptRow at web/account.js:228-259. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q12 Brief rows on My Perch look alike: Student rows are all "Options checked <date>", so two briefs on one day share a title, in web/account.js:263. Researcher rows show topics or "Researcher brief, <date>", never the researcher, in w1280-s49a-home.png. Add the time to student rows. Put the researcher's public display name first on researcher rows. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q13 "Change details and run again" puts the button above the fields: On w1280-s49a-rerun.png, "Build brief" sits at the top. The fields the user came to change are below it, and the form ends with no button. Add a second "Build brief" at the foot of the form. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q14 On a phone, 17 school chips come before the first award: In w360-s49b-awards.png the first award starts below the first screen. Below 420 px wide, show the schools as a "School" select beside "Level of study". Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q15 Headings show a blue focus box after navigation: It shows on Welcome in w1280-s49b-welcome.png and on Temple awards in w360-s49b-awards.png. A heading that gets focus from code should not show the ring. Use :focus-visible, or no outline on [tabindex="-1"] headings. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q16 Lead titles wrap at half the card width: On the researcher brief, the match pill, Keep and Dismiss take the right half, in w1280-s49a-brief-researcher.png. Titles break into three lines. Put Keep and Dismiss on a row under the facts at every width, and keep only the pill beside the title. Effort: small to medium. When: before the gate.
  • Q17 Canary tokens show on screen: The brief's "Your interests" shows "Canary: PERCH-CANARY-UG-INT-6W1J" in w1280-brief-student-profile.png. On stage this reads like a bug. Hide the canary line in on-screen text only. Keep it in stored text, exports and the leak checks, as rule 11 needs. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q18 The hand-off wait still hides the code-written parts: While the model writes, the box lists the leads, in w1280-handoff-busy.png. It does not show the subject or the draft body. Show the code-written subject, lead list and ERA line in the draft box at once. Let the model's opening paragraph fill in when it arrives. This closes the rest of P7. Effort: medium. When: after Demo Day.
  • Q19 A stored CV is unticked when a researcher builds: On w1280-s49a-pick-cv.png the stored "cv.md" is unticked, so cover points and Scout run without it. A signed-in researcher agreed to CV use at sign-up. Tick a stored CV by default. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q20 Lower-case titles, looked at again: "academic scholarships" and "micro grants" still look unfinished, in w1280-s49b-awards-signed.png and w1280-s49a-route-t.png. Round 1 declined a fix because a title is copied text. A CSS ::first-letter capital changes only the display. The record, copy, export and evidence panel stay exact. Effort: small. When: before the gate, if the owner agrees.
  • Q21 The awards right column wraps "No amount or deadline on the page": It takes two lines in a narrow column, in w1280-s49b-awards-signed.png. Use "Not on the page" there. Keep the full sentence in the evidence panel. Effort: small. When: before the gate.

Features to add

  • Q22 One click to a finished researcher brief: The researcher side of the landing has only Find, and a live brief takes about 38 s, per tracker row 77. A judge with three minutes will not wait. Add "See an example brief" under Find. There are two ways to back it. The nightly precache in the scheduler at perch/jobs.py:659-725 covers route A only, as perch/service.py:417 shows, so a precached brief is instant only with explanations off. The static replay page that scripts/export_replay.py builds is complete, costs nothing and cannot stall. Recommendation: link the replay of a PI-4 brief, and keep Q38's stored briefs as the signed-in version. The researcher id comes from deploy config, never from tracked code. Effort: medium. When: before the gate.
  • Q23 "Has a deadline" and "Has an amount" filters, F4: Most rows in the dense awards list say "No amount or deadline on the page", in w1280-s49b-awards-signed.png. A student who wants money they can act on should be able to hide those. Code reads the record fields. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q24 Ask Scout about one card: Scout lives on its own tab, away from the cards. Add "Ask Scout about this" to each card's menu. It opens the Scout tab with "Tell me about <title>" typed in. This is the cheap slice of round 1's D4. Effort: small. When: after Demo Day.
  • Q25 A calendar file of dated kept items, F2: My Perch already sorts kept items by date. Offer an .ics download with one event per stated date. Every date is copied from the record. Items with no date are listed by name and left out. Effort: medium. When: after Demo Day.
  • Q26 A graduate sample student, F5: A graduate guest can only try the undergraduate sample. Add a SYNTHETIC, canary-tagged graduate persona and let the guest pick one, as rule 12 allows. Effort: medium. When: after Demo Day.
  • Q27 Delete one brief, F6: Today the only way to remove a brief is to delete the account. Build the cascading delete that round 1 described: cover points, drafts and the Scout session go with it. Effort: medium. When: after Demo Day.
  • Q28 Leave out a paper that is not mine, F10: OpenAlex sometimes credits a researcher with another person's paper. Let the user untick it on "What Perch read" and run again. Effort: medium. When: after Demo Day.
  • Q29 An agency filter on the funding list: Researchers think in agencies, such as NSF or NIH, not in levels of study. Add an "Agency" select read from the record's agency field. Effort: small. When: after Demo Day.

Remove

  • Q30 "Level of study" on the research funding list: A faculty researcher has no level of study. The select shows on #/funding in w1280-s49b-funding.png, from web/browse.js:318-322. Hide it when the audience is researcher. Q29 replaces it. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q31 "Explain each lead" on the first screen: The checkbox on w1280-s49a-pick-cv.png exposes a cost switch. A judge who unticks it gets cards with no reasons. Move it into "Tell Perch more" and keep it on by default. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q32 The "Instrument or relationship" column when every row says "Grant": In w1280-s49b-compare.png the column reads "Grant, funding instrument" on every row. Hide a column when every cell is the same, and say so in one line under the table. This is round 1's deferred U45. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
  • Q33 "Records as JSON" for students, R2: A student does not need JSON, in w1280-brief-student-export.png. Drop it from the student Export menu. Effort: small. When: before the gate.

Flow redesigns

  • Q34 One shortlist across Perch: Today there are two lists. Keep on a browse row goes to the saved list on My Perch. Keep on a brief card goes to that brief's shortlist. Only the brief's list reaches Compare and the hand-off, so an award saved from browsing can never be drafted to an office. Merge them into one shortlist per side. Give My Perch "Compare and draft" over that list, grouped by office. Effort: large. When: after Demo Day. The cheap slice for now is Q11.
  • Q35 Browse with fit, for students, round 1 D2: The awards list and the fit check are still two screens with a choice on the landing. Merge them so the awards list shows each card's rule verdict for a signed-in student with a CV, and offers "Sort by fit". Effort: large. When: after Demo Day. A cheap slice for today: on the awards list, a signed-in student with a CV sees one bar, "Check these against your CV", that opens the student brief.
  • Q36 A "Next steps" tab, round 1 D3: Rename Compare to "Next steps". Show, in order, the table, the calendar file from Q25, and the hand-off. That is the order a person acts in. Effort: medium. When: after Demo Day.
  • Q37 Code-only notes for guests, a fork for Dakshitha: The student note to the fellowships office is written by code with no model, as w1280-s49-student-compare.png says. A guest's note would cost nothing and store nothing. The 2026-11-04 decision keeps all drafts account-only. Recommendation: keep the rule for Demo Day and use Q7's examples. After Demo Day, let guests get the code-only student note and the code-written part of the researcher draft. Effort: small to build, once decided. When: after Demo Day.
  • Q38 A presenter path that skips setup: The presenter signs in, lands on My Perch, switches side, opens a brief, and loads the sample student. Each step is a chance to stall on stage. Give the demo-presenter account one stored student brief and one researcher brief, built before the talk. Open each from My Perch with one press. This needs no code, only a run-sheet step and a check on the morning of the demo. Effort: small. When: before the gate.
S49 design: round 1 build spec (2026-11-04)docs/design/S49_DESIGN.md, 4 Nov 2026

This spec turns five front-end documents into one build for round 1. The five are S48_UI_NOTES.md, S48_UI_DESIGN.md, S48_UI_REVIEW.md, S49_UIUX_REVIEW.md and S49_PRODUCT_REVIEW.md. It also builds the four S49 decisions in docs/DECISIONS.md. Item codes refer to those documents:

  • D1 to D5: sections of S48_UI_DESIGN.md.
  • M1 to M6: the must-fix items of S48_UI_REVIEW.md.
  • U1 to U55: items of S49_UIUX_REVIEW.md.
  • P, S, F, R and D codes with a "P-" prefix: items of S49_PRODUCT_REVIEW.md. For example P-D1 is its flow redesign D1.
  • FM codes: items of S49_FUNCTION_REVIEW.md. For example FM3 is its M3.

The walk researcher is PI-4 (A5026494099). No other researcher is named here.

1. Decisions

Dakshitha delegated S49 decisions to Perch-dev. The design forks below are settled here. Each one goes into docs/DECISIONS.md when the orchestrator records this spec.

  • Lowercase Temple titles stay as the page wrote them (U50 over S2): a title is copied record text. Changing it, even its first letter, breaks the copy-only spirit of rule 3. The lowercase titles go to round 2 as a data-quality item for the Temple page parser.
  • Closed calls are hidden by default on the funding list only (P2): the "Show closed calls" switch is off by default on #/funding. The awards list hides nothing by date. The reason is the past-cycle decision: 22 Temple awards show last cycle's date and most of them recur. Hiding them by date would undo that decision.
  • A past date on an award reads as a past date, not "Closed": on the awards list, an award whose date has passed gets the muted tag "Past date on the page". Funding keeps the "Closed" tag, because a Grants.gov close date is final. Both are written by code from the record's own date.
  • Temple internal funding is a third route button (route: "T"): it sits between Grants and Industry, as "Temple internal". It matches the existing switch pattern, and it keeps those calls in their own list, as the decision asks. Section 3.4 has the contract.
  • My Perch is the signed-in home (P-D1, U41): a signed-in user's #/ shows My Perch. The hero landing moves to #/start for signed-in users. Guests and signed-out visitors keep the hero at #/.
  • The saved list holds saved awards and kept leads together (P1, F1, F3): My Perch lists both, in one list sorted by date. One server call returns both, so the page needs no fan-out over briefs.
  • Industry leads stay off My Perch: they hold no date and they are inferences. They stay inside their brief, with their "inferred" label.
  • Samples cannot be saved (rule 11): the server refuses an id from the SYNTHETIC corpus. The sample screen shows no Keep button.
  • Guests get no Keep button on the lists: a guest saves nothing. Instead, one line above the list says to sign in.
  • Cover-letter points for guests are offered once per list (U16, S9): guests see one line above the list and nothing on each card.
  • The "withheld explanation" message appears once per list (U3): each card keeps one quiet line.
  • The finished brief folds its progress card into a chip (U37, S8): the chip reads "Ready · 7 s" and sits beside Export. It opens the Steps. While a brief builds or after it fails, the full card stays.
  • Form screens use one centred column (U31): welcome, account, the student start, and Find and pick use a centred 760 px column. Lists, briefs and My Perch use the full 1180 px page column (U7).
  • Lead cards put the title first, on both sides: the agency, the code and the program move into one muted line under the title. Closes and Amount are always shown, with a muted "Not stated" when missing. This removes the empty-tag bug (M1) for good.
  • Browse lists use dense rows (U38): the title and the line under it go on the left. Amount and deadline go in a fixed right column. Keep and an icon link to the source go at the far right.
  • Default sort per list (P3): awards sort "A to Z". Most awards state no date, so a date sort would bury them. Funding sorts by "Closing soonest", which puts open calls first.
  • School counts are hidden while a search or level is set (U1): this is a front-end fix. /filters stays as it is.
  • The page's own deadline words are shown when there is no date (FM3): deadline_quote is already in the browse and brief payloads. The card shows it in quotes under "Deadline", so it never claims "Not stated".
  • P6 waits for round 2: the "what the rules checked" line needs rule output that the server does not yet return, and the product review asks for a live capture first (S15).
  • The hand-off progress (P7) uses the cheap version, in Tier B: while the model writes, the box lists the kept lead titles and the office name it already has. There is no server change.

For Dakshitha

  • None this round. Every fork above is settled under the S49 delegation. One item needs the orchestrator, not a design choice: route T depends on the back-end function package (FM9). If that package does not ship route T in round 1, FE-A item A9 and BE-S item V6 are dropped.

2. Scope for round 1

The budget is about 6 hours of builder time, run by 3 builders in parallel at about 2 hours each. Each package lists its items in build order with minute estimates. Tier A must ship. Tier B ships only if the package is under budget. A builder cuts from the bottom of Tier B first.

  • Tier A adds up to about 410 minutes: FE-A is about 140, FE-B about 145 and BE-S about 125. That is about 7 hours, one hour over the target. The must-fix items and the four decisions alone need about 5 hours.
  • The cut line, if the orchestrator holds to 6 hours: move these to round 2, in this order.
    • FE-A A5's ready chip: keep the tab names and the button label, and leave the progress card as it is. This saves 15 minutes.
    • FE-B B4's documents card: My Perch keeps two cards. This saves 8 minutes.
    • FE-B B3's sort select: keep the "Show closed calls" switch, and keep funding sorted by closing date with no control. This saves 10 minutes. BE-S V1 still ships open_only and sort. browse.js still sends sort=closing on #/funding, because the server's default is name.
    • FE-A A8's pick-screen link: keep the rerun route. This saves 5 minutes.
    • BE-S S1's student card restyle: keep the withheld line and the deadline quote only. This saves 8 minutes.
  • Why the target slips: the must-fix list grew by six product items and four decisions after the S48 design was sized.

Must-fix coverage

Every must-fix item from the five documents is in Tier A:

  • S48 notes and design:
    • D1 is FE-A A2.
    • D2 is BE-S S6.
    • D3 is FE-A A7.
    • D4 is FE-A A8 with FE-B B4.

    • U3 is FE-A A5 and BE-S S2.

  • Product review:

    • P4 is BE-S V5 with FE-A A3.

Deferred to round 2, with reasons

  • U40, cover points in two columns: this is a layout rebuild of pointsBlock. Round 1 already changes that block for U14 and U15.
  • U46, U47 and U48, profile polish: the profile tab is not on the demo's main path. U46 is FE-A Tier B.
  • U20, U51 and U52, Scout layout: these are polish only, and Scout's chat sizing is fragile. U21 ships.

  • F6, delete one brief: a brief owns cover points, hand-off drafts and a Scout session. A one-row delete would leave those behind. A cascading delete needs its own design and tests.

  • S48 review should-fix left for round 2: splitting the funder and activity-code filter chips, short labels and no indent for cover-point citations (with U40), and an honest match count per section. Each needs a closer look at the data first.

3. Build packages

3.0 Step 0, done by the orchestrator before any builder starts (about 10 minutes, one commit)

These changes let three worktrees build in parallel without touching each other's files.

  • New stylesheet: create web/pages.css with one comment line, /* S49: page styles owned by FE-B. Loaded after styles.css. */.
  • Link it: in web/index.html, add <link rel="stylesheet" href="pages.css"> right after the styles.css link.
  • Preview script: in scripts/build_ui_preview.py, inline pages.css after styles.css, the same way styles.css is inlined.
  • Stub for cover notices: in web/cover.js, add export function coverListLine() { return null; }. FE-A and BE-S import it. FE-B replaces the body.
  • Walk flow loader: at the end of scripts/ux_walk.py, before main, add a loader:
    • What it imports: every scripts/walk_flows/*.py.
    • What each module must define: register(U) -> tuple[dict, list]. Here U is the ux_walk module, from sys.modules[__name__]. The tuple holds the module's flows and its plant names.
    • What it merges: the flows into FLOWS and the plant names into PLANTS, before argparse reads them.
    • The folder: create scripts/walk_flows/__init__.py empty.
  • Check the new files are served: the app serves web/ through a directory mount (WebFiles) and the CSP has style-src 'self'. After the commit, confirm with one curl that GET /pages.css returns 200 from the dev server.
  • Who owns which flow file: FE-A owns scripts/walk_flows/s49_fe_a.py. FE-B owns scripts/walk_flows/s49_fe_b.py. BE-S owns scripts/walk_flows/s49_be_s.py.

3.1 Rules for every package

  • Isolation: each package is built in its own worktree (isolation: "worktree"). It touches only the files it owns. Never switch branches in the main checkout, because the v1 deploy runs from it.
  • Fail first: every new walk check is written before the code change. The builder runs it on the untouched worktree, records FAIL, implements, then records PASS. Both results and the base commit go in the commit message body as fail-first: <check> FAIL on <sha>, PASS after. A check that cannot fail on the old code is not a check: rewrite it.
  • Walk runs: one walk server runs at a time on port 8191. Start it from your own worktree with scripts/run_limited.sh. Use --only <your flows> and stop the server when done.
  • Existing checks: existing walk checks that your change breaks on purpose are updated in your own flow file, never in another package's file. Example: the scoutmarks flagged text, or landing assuming #/ is the hero for signed-in users. If the old check lives in ux_walk.py, tell the orchestrator. It edits ux_walk.py after the merge.
  • Tests: make test passes in your worktree before you hand back. FE-A owns tests/test_web.py. FE-B writes new tests only in tests/test_web_pages.py. BE-S writes new tests in tests/test_saved.py, tests/test_browse_sort.py and in the existing compare and export tests.
  • Copy: all copy in this spec is final. Remove the "DRAFT copy … for Dakshitha to review" comments in the files you touch.
  • Commits: small commits with the project's attribution trailer, as given in the orchestrator's brief. No session links in commit messages.
  • Escalate instead of guessing: escalate any record field you would have to invent, any office name not in perch/offices.py, any number not from a record, and any change to a file you do not own.

3.2 Shared contracts

Hash routes (FE-A builds them; FE-B links to them)
  • #/:
    • Signed in, welcome done: My Perch home. FE-A's route() calls renderMyPerch(main(), rt, { home: true }) with screen("home").
    • Everyone else: the hero landing, as now.
  • #/me: the same My Perch home, with screen("home").
  • #/start: the hero landing (renderFind) for anyone. On first entry, a signed-in user's S.who follows session.audience.
  • #/find: as now. When there are no candidates, renderPick redirects to #/start, not to #/.
  • #/rerun/<briefId>: loads the brief with api.brief(id). Then:
    • Student brief: goReplace("#/student"). The start screen shows the stored CV and entries, ready to edit.
    • Researcher brief: fills S.find from the brief and goes with goReplace("#/find"), the pick screen with the person already picked. Section A8 has the details.
  • The wordmark links to #/ as now. That is My Perch for a signed-in user.
Card markup (FE-A styles it; FE-A and BE-S emit it)
(list item) .card.lead[.kept][.gone][.is-sample][data-id]
  div.lead-top
    div.lead-name
      h3.lead-title > button.title-btn > span(title) + evMark()
      p.lead-sub            muted line; parts joined by " · "; may hold span.tag.sample / span.tag.ember
    div.lead-end            verdict chip (student only), match pill, div.actions (Keep, Dismiss | Restore)
  dl.facts.facts-2          always two div.fact: [Closes | Deadline] and [Amount]
  ...notes, reasons, explanation...
  p.withheld-line           only on a flagged card (replaces the amber box)
  div.cover                 cover.js
  • The title fallback is "Untitled opportunity", never the record id (D5).
  • A missing fact is dd > span.missing with the text "Not stated".
  • A deadline with no date but a deadline_quote is dd > span.quote-date with the text The page says: “<deadline_quote>”. It applies to scholarships and Temple opportunities (FM3).
List header and notice slot (FE-A and BE-S emit it; FE-B fills it)

Each brief list, on both sides, renders this above its ol.leads:

div.list-head
  h2.section-title#routes-title        the count heading
  div.sort-group                       the existing Sort switch
p.hint.model-line                      researcher grants only: "Model text is a model's reading of the fit, checked against the records it cites."
div#list-notices
  p.notice.info.list-note              only when two or more visible cards are flagged
  <coverListLine(ctx) result>          from cover.js; null when there is nothing to say
  • The flagged note text: "Some written reasons failed Perch’s citation check, so they are left out. Every date, amount and rule result on the cards is still copied from the record."
  • The per-card withheld line: p.hint.withheld-line with the text "Written reason withheld: it failed the citation check."
coverListLine(ctx) (FE-B builds it in cover.js)
  • Input: ctx is the same object coverBlock takes.
  • Returns for a guest: p.list-note holding icon("pen"), the text "Cover-letter points need an account. ", and a[href=ctx.signIn] with the text "Sign in".
  • Returns after a daily-allowance error in this page view: p.notice.info.list-note[role=status] holding the server's message and, when /usage answered, " It comes back at <time>." The time is resets_at formatted in local time, hour and minute. If it is not today, a short date comes first.
  • Returns otherwise: null.
  • Redraw: on a quota error, cover.js redraws #list-notices itself with document.getElementById("list-notices"). If that element is missing, it falls back to the per-card error, as now.
Student offices in the brief (BE-S builds and reads it; FE-A passes it)
  • BE-S, server side: GET /briefs/{id} adds offices for student briefs only:
"offices": {
  "F": {"key": "sdfa", "name": "Scholar Development and Fellowships Advising", "url": "https://undergraduate.temple.edu/fellowships"},
  "S": {"key": "sfs", "name": "Student Financial Services", "url": "https://sfs.temple.edu/"}
}

The values come from perch/offices.py for_route("F") and for_route("S"). Nothing is typed by hand.

  • FE-A: renderStudentPanel passes offices: S.brief.offices || api.studentOffices.
  • BE-S, student.js: officeName already reads ctx.offices[r].name. No change is needed beyond checking it.
Saved list API (BE-S builds it; FE-B calls it)

All three routes need a signed-in account. A guest gets 403 {"error": "account_required"}. POST and DELETE need the CSRF header and consent (_consented). audience works as on /me/docs, through _side: the session's side when it is left out. _side does not check the account's roles, so the front end chooses the side:

  • Saving from a list: browse.js sends the list's own side (student on #/awards, researcher on #/funding) when the account has that role. Otherwise it sends the session's side, so the item shows on the My Perch the user can open.
  • Reading on My Perch: the "Kept and saved" card calls api.saved(side) for the side shown, and reloads when the side switch changes.

GET /me/saved?audience=student returns 200:

{
  "audience": "student",
  "total": 2,
  "items": [
    {
      "record_id": "temple_pages:example-award",
      "saved_id": "6f1c…-uuid",
      "saved_at": "2026-11-04T21:10:00+00:00",
      "kept_in": [{"brief_id": "9a2e…-uuid", "built_at": "2026-11-03T18:00:00+00:00"}],
      "record": { "...": "the browse item() shape: the record's own fields plus kind, scope, schools, levels, deadline, amount_max, sample, source, source_url, fetched_at" }
    },
    {
      "record_id": "grants_gov:12345",
      "saved_id": null,
      "saved_at": null,
      "kept_in": [{"brief_id": "9a2e…-uuid", "built_at": "2026-11-03T18:00:00+00:00"}],
      "record": null
    }
  ]
}
  • What it holds: one item per record_id. That is every saved_item row of the side, plus every lead with status kept in the side's stored briefs.
  • Kept leads included: kind opportunity or scholarship only, never sample.
  • saved_id: null when the record is only kept in a brief.
  • record: looked up in the public store at read time. It is null when the store no longer holds it.
  • Order: first, items whose record.deadline is today or later, by date ascending. Then past dates, newest first. Then items with no date, then items with no record. Ties go by title, case-folded. The date is the record's deadline column from columns(r). Nothing is computed.

POST /me/saved?audience=student with body {"record_id": "temple_pages:example-award"}:

  • New: 201 {"saved_id": "<uuid>", "record_id": "...", "saved_at": "<iso>"}.
  • Already saved: 200 with the same shape. The call is idempotent.
  • Unknown record: 404 {"error": "not_found"}.
  • A SYNTHETIC record, by source synthetic or an id starting sample:: 422 {"error": "sample_not_saved"}.
  • More than 200 saved on the side: 409 {"error": "saved_full"}.
  • Storage: the row is stored as SavedItem (kind saved_item), encrypted like every user row. It is never logged with its record id in plain text beside the user id.

DELETE /me/saved/{saved_id} returns 200 {"ok": true}, or 404 {"error": "not_found"}.

Browse parameters (BE-S builds them; FE-B sends them)

Both GET /awards and GET /opportunities gain two parameters:

  • sort: name (the default and the current order), closing or amount.
    • closing: dates today or later ascending, then past dates newest first, then no date. Ties go by name, then id.
    • amount: amount_max descending, with nulls last. Ties go by name, then id.
  • open_only: a bool, false by default. When true, it keeps deadline IS NULL OR deadline >= today, using the server's date.
  • The cursor stays opaque to the front end. For closing and amount, it may be an offset token. The lists hold under 1,000 rows.
  • The response gains "sort": "<the sort used>". Nothing else changes.
Brief summaries (BE-S builds them; FE-B reads them)
  • New fields in each GET /me/briefs item: "kept", the number of kept public leads, and "sample_kept".
Compare rows (BE-S builds them; FE-B reads them)
  • The row title: each rows[] item's title is the title alone, such as "MPS Chemistry Research Programs".
  • The number: a new field, "number", holds the opportunity number or null.
  • Export: perch/export.py prints "<number>: <title>" when there is a number, so the export reads as before.

3.3 Package FE-A: brief screen, lead cards, landing, header, routing, base styles

Files FE-A may touch:

  • web/app.js
  • web/styles.css
  • tests/test_web.py
  • scripts/walk_flows/s49_fe_a.py

Budget: Tier A is about 140 minutes. FE-A is the critical path, so it starts first.

A1. Base stylesheet pass (25 minutes)

Do this first, as its own commit.

  • Merge duplicate rules (U53): fold the duplicates so each selector is defined once, at its first location.
    • .cite: lines about 135, 1116, 1127, 1221 and 1455 become one rule.
    • .tag.sample: lines about 443 and 882 become one rule.
    • .foot p: lines about 443 and 967 become one rule.
    • Commit message: list the computed values that changed. There should be none.
  • New tokens on :root:
    • --page: 1180px
    • --form: 760px
    • --fs-12: 12px; --fs-14: 14px; --fs-16: 16px; --fs-19: 19px; --fs-24: 24px
    • --s-1: 4px; --s-2: 8px; --s-3: 12px; --s-4: 16px; --s-5: 24px; --s-6: 32px
  • One left edge (U7): all four containers are max-width: calc(var(--page) + 32px); margin: 0 auto; padding-left: 16px; padding-right: 16px.
    • The four: .bar-in, #banner p, main, and .foot p with .foot .promises.
    • main by screen:
    • body[data-screen="list"], "brief" and "home" use the page width.
    • body[data-screen="form"] uses max-width: calc(var(--form) + 32px), centred, with padding-top: 32px (U31, U32).
    • "landing" stays 712 px and "help" stays 852 px.

Budget: Tier A is about 145 minutes.

B1. api.js (5 minutes)

Add these methods:

  • saved: (side = null) => p(\/me/saved${query({ audience: side })}\)
  • save: (recordId, side = null) => post(\/me/saved${query({ audience: side })}\, { record_id: recordId })
  • unsave: (savedId) => p(\/me/saved/${encodeURIComponent(savedId)}\, { method: "DELETE" })
  • usage: () => p("/usage")
  • samples(audienceName, cursor, limit): an optional limit, for Tier B S14.
  • list(kind, params): this already passes any params. Callers add sort and open_only.
B2. pages.css base (3 minutes)
  • Section comments: add one fenced comment per screen in the order of this package.
  • Type scale: use the tokens FE-A adds (--fs-*, --s-*). Until the merge, write the literal values with the token as a fallback, for example font-size: var(--fs-14, 14px).

    blockquote.ar-quote   first eligibility quote, clamped to 2 lines (-webkit-line-clamp: 2)

    dl  dt "Amount" dd …    dt "Deadline"|"Closes" dd …

3.6 Merge order and the run-through

  1. Step 0 (orchestrator).
  2. Merge BE-S first. The others rely on its routes and fields.
  3. Merge FE-A next. It owns the routes and the base styles.
  4. Merge FE-B last.
  5. After the merge:
    • The orchestrator updates the two old checks in ux_walk.py: CHECKED_FLAGGED, and landing's signed-in assumption.
    • Then QA runs the full walk at 1280 and 360, in light and dark.
    • QA opens every changed screenshot.

4. Help page (web/help.js, FE-B)

Every sentence below is true of the code after round 1. FE-B checks each one against the merged code before it closes B10.

  • Keep from the lists: "On Temple awards and Research funding, Keep saves a record to your account. Kept and saved records collect on My Perch with their dates. Sample records cannot be kept."
  • Sort and closed calls: "Sort a list A to Z, by the soonest date or by the largest amount. Records that state no date or amount come last. Research funding hides calls whose close date has passed; turn on Show closed calls to see them."
  • A past date on an award: "Many Temple awards recur each year. When an award’s page shows a date that has passed, the card says Past date on the page, and a check of your fit says may be eligible, with the date from the page. Check the page for this year’s date."
  • My Perch as home: "When you are signed in, Perch opens on My Perch: what you kept and saved, sorted by date, your briefs, and your documents. Start a new search from there."
  • Change details and run again: "Change details and run again opens the start screen with your details filled in. Running it makes a new brief; the old one stays on My Perch."
  • The researcher CV: "A researcher may add a CV before building a brief. It is optional. Perch uses it for cover-letter points and Scout, stores it encrypted, and blanks contact details before a model reads it."
  • Temple internal (only if A9 ships): "A researcher brief may show a third list, Temple internal: Temple’s own funding calls for faculty. They are kept apart from federal grants. Each call’s page says whom to contact."
  • The lead card (update the anatomy figure and its callouts): "The title comes first, then the agency and code. Closes and Amount are always shown; Not stated means the record leaves it blank. The page says means the date is in the page’s words, not a date field."
  • Model text: "Model text marks a model’s sentence, checked against the records it cites. When a sentence fails that check twice, the card says so in one line and keeps only the fields copied from the record."
  • Cover-letter points: keep COVER_HELP. Add: "When today’s allowance is used, one note above the list says so, with the time it comes back."
  • Scout: keep the line that Scout can read your saved list. It is now true.
  • Sample data: keep the existing sample-data paragraph. Add "Sample records cannot be kept or saved."
S49 product and flow review (fresh context, 2026-11-04)docs/design/S49_PRODUCT_REVIEW.md, 4 Nov 2026

Read-only review of the v1 web app on rebuild/v1. Inputs: the S48 walk screenshots in build/s48_walk_light/ and build/s48_walk_handoff/, the front-end code in web/, and the routes in perch/api.py, perch/browse/routes.py and perch/user/routes.py. Items already queued in S48_UI_NOTES.md and S48_UI_DESIGN.md are not repeated.

Four readers were kept in mind:

  • Undergraduate: wants money for next year, fast, with deadlines they can act on.
  • Graduate student: wants fellowships and graduate awards, and is unsure which side of Perch they belong to.
  • Faculty researcher: wants open grants that fit their papers, and a clean path to the research office.
  • Demo Day judge: has three minutes and needs to see one finished, cited result.

One caution first. The walk ran the fake model, as scripts/walk_server.py:1 says. So the model text in the screenshots is not real. The repeated "explanation was withheld" banners, the generic grant sentence and the "first topic area" chips are fake-model output. They are not filed as product bugs here.

The error and account states were checked and work: the list error with Retry, the sign-in-down notice, the delete dialog that asks the user to type "delete", and the "Your data was deleted" notice. They are in w1280-researcher-list-error.png, w1280-signin-unavailable.png, w1280-delete-dialog.png and w1280-after-delete.png. The only issues found there are R5 and the "saved awards" text in P1.

Must-fix (flow breaks or confuses)

  • P1 The saved list is promised but never built: No route writes a saved_item; only perch/scout/job.py:103 reads one. Yet Scout says it can "Read your saved list" in web/scout.js:21 and web/scout.js:30. The guest My Perch line promises "saved awards" in web/account.js:241. The delete text lists "saved awards" in web/account.js:158 and web/account.js:225. Build Keep on browse cards, as in F1, or remove every claim, as in R1. Effort: medium to build, small to remove.
  • P2 Research funding opens on closed, stale calls: The list is sorted by title. So the first cards a researcher sees are a 2020/2021 call and a call that closed in February 2022, in w1280-funding.png. Temple-only shows calls that closed in 2021, 2022 and 2024, in w1280-funding-temple.png. Hide records whose close date has passed by default, and add a "Show closed" switch. Code can do this from close_date alone. Effort: medium.
  • P3 Browse lists have no sort: web/browse.js has no sort control, and the order is by title. Add "Closing soonest" and "Largest amount", both read from record fields. Records with no date or amount go last. Effort: medium.
  • P4 The student hand-off hides the office name from guests: A guest sees "The Temple office for this route" in the radio and in every table row, in w1280-brief-student-compare.png. The fallback is in web/student.js:435. The office names are public constants in perch/offices.py, such as Scholar Development and Fellowships Advising. Send them with the brief so guests see the real name. Effort: small.
  • P5 Compare shows the hand-off before the comparison: Under the heading "Compare 2 kept leads", the hand-off form comes first and the table comes after it, in w1280-brief-researcher-compare.png. A person compares first, then decides where to send. Put the table first and the hand-off below it. Effort: small.
  • P6 A "May be eligible" card with no gaps says nothing: The text above the list says "may be eligible" is the best verdict Perch can give, in w1280-brief-student.png. When a card has rule gaps, the "Still needed" line in web/student.js:345 explains it. When it has none, the chip stands alone and tells the student nothing. Add one line saying what the rules checked, such as "Level checked; the listing states no deadline". Every word comes from the rule results in perch/student.py. Confirm on the live capture in S15, since the walk brief is seeded. Effort: small.
  • P7 The hand-off wait has no progress: The hint says the draft can take up to two minutes, in web/handoff.js:93. During that time the screen shows a greyed button and one status line, in w1280-handoff-busy.png. Show the code-written parts of the draft at once: the subject, the lead list and the ERA line. Let the model's opening paragraph fill in when it arrives. Effort: medium.
  • P8 A returning user lands on the guest-style landing: A signed-in user sees the same hero and buttons as a new visitor, in w1280-after-welcome.png. My Perch is reachable only through the name menu, in web/app.js:276. Put "My Perch" in the header, and add "Open your last brief" to the landing. Effort: small.

Should-fix

  • S1 Browse cards spend two rows on "Not stated": Most of the 360 Temple awards show "Amount: Not stated" and "Deadline: Not stated", in w1280-awards.png. The rows are drawn even when empty, in web/browse.js:101 to web/browse.js:104. When both are empty, show one quiet line: "Amount and deadline are not on the page." Effort: small.
  • S2 Some award titles are lower case: "academic scholarships" and "additional scholarships for sophomores, juniors and seniors" look unfinished, in w1280-awards.png. Capitalise the first letter when showing the title. Leave the stored record as it is. Effort: small.
  • S3 The brief tabs have different names on each side: The researcher brief says "Profile". The student brief says "What Perch read" on desktop and "Read" on a phone. Use one name, "What Perch read", on both sides. Effort: small.
  • S4 The match number is not explained: Cards show "Match good 69" with no scale, in w1280-brief-student.png. Add a short hint saying what the number counts and its range. Check the wording against perch/score.py. Effort: small.
  • S5 A ten-year-old date is the biggest thing on the profile: The award horizon shows "30 Jun 2016, already passed" in large type, in w1280-brief-researcher-profile.png. When the date has passed, show it at normal size under a plain line: "No running federal award found." Effort: small.
  • S6 Keep and Dismiss push the title down on a phone: At 360 px the buttons sit above the title, so each card starts with buttons, in w360-brief-student.png. Move Keep and Dismiss to the foot of the card on narrow screens. Effort: small.
  • S7 Compare rows start with the opportunity number: Rows read "26-519: MPS Chemistry Research Programs", in w1280-brief-researcher-compare.png. Show the title first and the number on a second, quieter line. Effort: small.
  • S8 The progress card stays large after the brief is ready: "Brief ready" with a full bar takes about 75 px at the top of every tab, in w1280-brief-researcher.png. Once done, shrink it to one line: "Built in 7 s · Steps". Effort: small.
  • S9 Guests see the same sign-in button on every card: "Sign in to get cover-letter points" repeats on all ten cards, in w1280-brief-student.png. Show it once above the list. Effort: small.
  • S10 Back from a brief ignores where the user came from: A student brief's Back always goes to the start form, in web/app.js:755. A user who opened it from My Perch expects to go back to My Perch. Use the last screen the user was on. Effort: small.
  • S11 The school chips are cut off with no cue: The row ends in "Boyer Colle" at the right edge, in w1280-awards.png. Users will not know more schools exist. Wrap the chips, or use a "School" menu like the level menu. Effort: small.
  • S12 "Sides" is project jargon: The account page says "Your sides", in w1280-account.png. Say "You use Perch as" instead. Effort: small.
  • S13 Graduate students do not know which box to tick: The welcome asks "I am a student" or "I am a researcher", in w1280-welcome.png. Add one hint: "Graduate students: pick Student for fellowships. Pick Researcher too if you have published papers." Effort: small.
  • S14 The sample records page is 500 cards long: w1280-samples.png lists every sample with no filter. Show about 10 samples with a note that more exist, or give the page the same filters as the awards list. Effort: small.
  • S15 Review rounds need one live brief capture: The walk ran the fake model, so no reviewer has seen real fit text, real cover points or a real hand-off. Capture one researcher brief and one student brief from the live deploy before S51 closes. Effort: small.

Features to add

  • F1 Keep an award straight from the browse list: Add Keep to every browse card for signed-in users. Store it as a saved_item, which the data model already defines in perch/user/models.py:17. Show kept awards on My Perch. This closes P1 and links browsing to the brief. Effort: medium.
  • F2 A calendar file of deadlines: Offer an .ics download of kept leads, one event per stated close date or deadline. Every date is copied from the record, and nothing is sent. Records with no date are left out and listed by name. Put it in the Export menu and on My Perch. Effort: medium.
  • F3 Upcoming deadlines on My Perch: List kept leads from all briefs, sorted by closing date, with the Closed tag when a date has passed. This is the reminder Perch can give without sending anything. Effort: medium.
  • F4 "Has a deadline" and "Has an amount" filters: Most Temple awards state neither. A student who wants actionable money should be able to show only records that state one. Code reads the record fields. Effort: small.
  • F5 A graduate sample persona: Only persona-ug exists, in perch/user/briefs.py:70. A graduate guest sees an undergraduate's results. Add a SYNTHETIC, canary-tagged persona-grad and let the guest pick one, as rule 12 allows. Effort: medium.
  • F6 Delete one brief: perch/user/routes.py has no route to delete a single brief. Today the only way to remove one is to delete the whole account. Add a Delete button on each My Perch row. Effort: small.
  • F7 A finished example for a first look: A replay page can already be built by scripts/export_replay.py. The app reads it from PERCH_REPLAY in web/app.js:2296. Publish one as a separate static page and link "See a finished example brief" from the landing. A judge or a new visitor then sees a cited result in one click. Effort: medium.
  • F8 Check my fit from a browse card: A signed-in student with a stored CV should be able to run the rules on one award from the browse list. The rule result appears on the card, with no model call. Effort: medium.
  • F9 Suggested questions in Scout: Scout opens with a list of its own tools in developer words, such as "Read one record in full", in w1280-scout-clean.png. Replace the list with three or four example questions as buttons, such as "Which kept awards close first?". Keep the tool list under "What I can do". Effort: small.
  • F10 Leave out a paper that is not mine: OpenAlex sometimes credits a researcher with someone else's papers. On the profile tab, let the user untick a paper. Untick a paper and the brief is built again without it. This fits with the queued "change details and run again". Effort: medium.

Features or text to remove

  • R1 Scout's "saved list" claim: Remove "Read your saved list" from web/scout.js:21, web/scout.js:30 and web/scout.js:33 until F1 ships. Do the same for "saved awards" in web/account.js:241. Effort: small.
  • R2 "Records as JSON" for students: A student does not need JSON, in w1280-brief-student-export.png. Keep it for researchers, or move it under "More formats". Effort: small.
  • R3 Short opportunity numbers on funding cards: Lines such as "04" carry no meaning for a reader, in w1280-funding.png. Show the number in the evidence panel only. Effort: small.
  • R4 The "Unless a card says otherwise" box: Once S1 hides empty rows, the line "The listing states no deadline or amount" is redundant, in w1280-brief-student.png. Keep only the line about reading the award's own page. Effort: small.
  • R5 Two buttons that do the same thing when sign-in is down: "Try a sample student" and "Try it as a guest" both start a guest session, in w1280-signin-unavailable.png. Keep the button and drop the link line. Effort: small.
  • R6 The consent version line on the welcome screen: "Consent text, version 1." means nothing to a new user, in w1280-welcome.png. Keep it on the account page, where it already shows. Effort: small.

Flow redesigns proposed

  • D1 My Perch as the home screen for signed-in users: After sign-in, open My Perch, not the hero landing. It would hold upcoming deadlines from F3, kept items from F1, recent briefs and the CV status. The hero landing stays for guests and signed-out visitors. Effort: medium.
  • D2 Browse with fit, for students: Today a student chooses between "Browse Temple awards" and "Check my fit", and these are two separate screens. Merge them. The awards list is the main screen. A signed-in student with a CV sees the rule result on each card, plus a "Sort by fit" option. Guests see the plain list with a "Try the sample student" bar. This removes a decision on the landing. Effort: large.
  • D3 One "Next steps" tab: Rename Compare to "Next steps". In order, it would show the comparison table, the calendar file from F2, then the hand-off draft. That is the order a person acts in. Effort: medium.
  • D4 Scout beside the cards, not on its own tab: Today Scout lives on a separate tab, away from the cards it talks about. Add "Ask about this" on each card. It would open Scout in a side panel with that record already named. The tab can stay for open questions. Effort: large.
  • D5 Own CV for guests, a fork for Dakshitha: A guest undergraduate can only try the sample student, in web/student.js:77. Letting a guest paste a CV for the hour, never stored, would serve the main student job. The fit rules in perch/student.py are code, not a model. So a guest CV could get rule verdicts with no call to the provider. Only cover points and Scout would need the consent that rule 1 asks for. The open question is where the text lives during the hour. Recommendation: keep the sample-only guest until after Demo Day, then decide. Effort: medium.
S49 UI/UX review (fresh context, 2026-11-04)docs/design/S49_UIUX_REVIEW.md, 4 Nov 2026

This review covers about 30 screenshots from build/s48_walk_light and build/s48_walk_dark, at 1280 and 360 wide, and the owner's notes. Each item is traced to the code. File paths are under web/ unless they say otherwise. Items already queued in S48_UI_REVIEW.md or S48_UI_DESIGN.md are left out. Researchers are not named; "the researcher" means the walk's researcher brief.

Must-fix

  • U1 School chips show the wrong counts: a search for "zzzzqqxx" gives "0 matches", but the chips still read "CST 25" and "Fox School of Business 22". The counts come from the unfiltered list. Either recount them for the current search and level, or drop the numbers while a search is active. browse.js:206-212, w1280-awards-empty.
  • U2 Compare titles start with the record number: each row in the Compare table reads "26-519: MPS Chemistry…". The owner flagged this on the cards. The prefix is added on the server. Show the title alone, and put the number on a second muted line or in Evidence. perch/compare.py:122, w1280-brief-researcher-compare, w360-handoff-ready.
  • U3 One warning repeated on every student card: each student card shows the same amber box, "The explanation was withheld because it failed the citation checks twice." Five of these boxes in a row make the page look broken, and they are louder than the titles. Say it once above the list, using the existing .common-lines box. On each card, keep only a quiet one-line hint. student.js:346, app.js:1739, styles.css:1288, w1280-brief-student.
  • U4 The page scrollbar is invisible: scrollbar-color: transparent hides the page scrollbar. It only shows when the mouse is within 8 px of the right edge. Keyboard and touchpad users lose the cue for where they are on long lists. Remove the rule and the mousemove toggle. styles.css:79, app.js:2287-2288.
  • U5 The disabled office hint is unreadable: .office-opt.off sets opacity .6 on the whole row. That fades the hint "no kept industry leads" to about 2.5:1 contrast. That hint is the reason the option is off. Fade only the radio and the label, and keep the hint at full --ink-3. styles.css:845, w1280-handoff-busy.
  • U6 The daily-allowance error repeats per card: after the allowance is used, each card shows a red error. The allowance applies to the whole account. Show it once as a page-level info notice. The notice should say when the allowance comes back, if the server gives that time. cover.js:136-145, w1280-cover-error.

Should-fix

  • U7 Four different left edges: the header text starts at about 52 px, the guest banner at 66, list pages at 100, and the footer at 98. Give the banner, the footer and the main column the same container as .bar-in (1212 px wide with 16 px padding). styles.css:108, 967, 1253, w1280-signin-unavailable, w1280-my-perch.
  • U8 Step count said twice: the finished progress card reads "Built in 7 s · 8 of 8 steps" and then "Steps (8 of 8 done)". When the brief is done, drop the count from the Steps summary. app.js:880, app.js:922, w1280-brief-researcher.
  • U9 Disabled buttons show a busy cursor: .btn[disabled] uses cursor: progress. Disabled buttons such as Continue and Compare look like they are loading. Use not-allowed, and keep progress for aria-busy only. styles.css:117, w1280-welcome.

On the student side, the wider switch pushes Sort onto its own row on the left. Put Sort on the count row, the line that reads "10 options…", on both sides. app.js:1449, styles.css:1203, w1280-brief-student.
  • U11 Two names for one shortlist button: the shortlist button says "Compare and hand off" on the researcher side and "Compare and draft a note" on the student side. Use one verb pattern on both, for example "Compare and draft". app.js:1051.

S48 UI/UX review (fresh-context Opus, 2026-11-04)docs/design/S48_UI_REVIEW.md, 4 Nov 2026

34 screenshots from build/s48_walk_{light,dark} at both widths, plus Dakshitha's two note images, each traced to the code. File paths are under web/.

Must-fix

  • M1 Empty agency tag: the tag is drawn even when it has no text (app.js:1719). Draw it only when the text is non-empty, with .tag:empty{display:none} as a backstop.
  • M2 Citation chips stretch lines: inline .cite has min-height 44px (styles.css:1455, 1224), which makes uneven line gaps in card text, Scout and cover points. Make it inline with line-height: inherit; WCAG 2.5.8 exempts inline targets.
  • M3 Stored-documents card stretches: .box-grid stretches it (styles.css:991). Set align-items: start.
  • M4 Wrong text: the researcher's documents card points to "the Check my fit page" (app.js:642). Replace it with an upload control (owner note 4).
  • M5 Compare order: the hand-off form sits between "Compare 2 kept leads" and the table (compare.js:111-122). Put the table first.
  • M6 Cover points heading on phone: the chevron sits on its own line (styles.css:860). Set flex-wrap: nowrap and flex: 1 on the text.

Should-fix (lead card)

  • Card order: put the title first, then one subtitle line (agency and program), with the head as a grid. Move the record number to the evidence panel.
  • Missing values: show one two-fact list, Closes and Amount, with a muted "Not stated", on every card. Use one word, not both "Closes" and "Deadline".
  • Match pill: put it on the right on student cards too.
  • Phone header: keep tags and match on one row and the actions on a second row.
  • "Why it fits": stop it wrapping.
  • Cover button: close the gap above it.

Should-fix (other)

  • Chips and labels:
    • Split the funder and activity-code chips.
    • Give cover-point citations a short label, and drop the points list indent.
    • Make the match count honest per section.
    • Give the filter chips a visible overflow cue, or wrap them.
  • List order: sort funding open-first by closing date.
  • Controls:
    • Give search and select the same height.
    • Cut the student interests text at a word boundary with "…".
    • Style the disabled "Compare and hand off" as an outline, with the hint "Keep a lead first".
  • Page width: use one main content width on every page.

Nice-to-have

  • Heading focus: move the ring on headings after navigation further out.
  • Landing buttons: make them equal widths.
  • Account page: align the consent row and drop the last document row's border.
  • Phone hand-off box: cap its height.
  • Type scale: reduce it to 12/14/16/19/24.

No rule 10 or rule 11 problems; sample badges are on every synthetic surface.

S48 design: Dakshitha's notes (design pass, 2026-11-04)docs/design/S48_UI_DESIGN.md, 4 Nov 2026

The notes themselves are in S48_UI_NOTES.md.

  1. Landing in one laptop screen.
    • Footer line: "Your CV is encrypted and deletable."
    • Measured: the page is 860 px tall at 1280 wide.
    • Cuts: the owl art from 150 to 96 px, the landing gaps from 26 to 16 px, the h1 maximum from 56 to 48 px, and the promises row on one line. That saves about 130 px.
    • Short screens: under 740 px high, the owl is 72 px.
    • Disclaimer: the Grants.gov disclaimer stays word for word, as the API's terms ask.
    • Walk check: no vertical scroll at 1280×720 and 1366×768, on both tabs.
  2. Load sample on the signed-in student start.
    • Button: a quiet "Load sample" beside "Your CV", with the hint "Fills the boxes with an invented student. Nothing is saved until you press Save."
    • Text: a shortened SYNTHETIC persona-ug in web/sample_student.js, with its canary line and no contact details.
    • Marking: a "SYNTHETIC example" tag, removed when the student edits the text.
    • Existing text: if a box already has text, an inline confirm reads "Replace what you typed with the sample?" with Replace and Keep mine.
    • Stored CV: the button is hidden when a CV is already stored. Guests keep "Try a sample student".
  3. Researcher CV on the first visit.
    • Card: a visible card "Add your CV (optional)" above Build brief, with the hint "Used for cover-letter points and Scout. Stored encrypted. Contact details are blanked before a model reads it."
    • Route: it reuses POST /me/docs?audience=researcher. A saved document is ticked into the brief.
    • Guests: they see "Sign in to add your CV."
    • Decided by Dakshitha: optional.
  4. Change details and run again, both sides.
    • Where: a "Change details and run again" button in the brief header and on each My Perch row, for signed-in users.
    • What it does: it opens the start screen prefilled from the brief's options and stored documents. Running again makes a new brief; the old one stays in My Perch with its saved leads.
    • Researcher: a "Choose someone else" link goes back to Find.
    • Guests: they keep "Start again".
  5. Cards.
    • Box grid: .box-grid { align-items: start }. The empty documents text becomes "No stored documents yet."
    • Lead card: draw the agency tag only when it has text, and hide an empty .tags.

    • Spacing: lead-card gaps are about 25% smaller. Closes and Award size share one row, and the model-text line is one line.
S46 design: a cover-letter points button on each leaddocs/design/S46_COVER_POINTS_DESIGN.md, 4 Nov 2026

Design pass, 2026-11-04. The /briefs/{id}/cover-points route works, but no screen calls it (S45 final re-check).

  • Where it goes. A "Cover-letter points" button in each lead card's action row, in app.js and student.js. It is hidden on dismissed cards. The result renders under the card's explanation. Compare, the evidence panel and Scout get no button.
  • Guests. A guest sees "Sign in to get cover-letter points", using the hand-off's sign-in link.
  • Button and hint. The label is "Cover-letter points" with a pen icon, and "Points again" once a result exists. The hint under it reads "A model writes these from your CV and papers. You put them in your own words."
  • While it runs. The button is disabled with aria-busy. A role=status line reads "A model is reading the record and your CV. This takes up to two minutes…". The page polls every 2 s, for about 150 s at most.
  • The result. It reuses scout.js pointsBlock, which is exported for this. That gives the Model text tag, the Sample data badge, the withheld notice, the citation chips and Copy the points. The block opens with focus on its summary, and the page announces "The points are ready below." A single GET on render brings back points that are already stored.
  • Errors, in role=alert:
    • 429 quota: the server's message.
    • 429 rate: "Too many requests. Try again in N seconds".
    • 409: "Cover points start once the brief has finished."
    • 403: the sign-in link.
    • A failed job or a timeout: "The points could not be made. Try again."
    • The button is re-enabled after any of these.
  • Samples. They are allowed and marked as samples by the existing badge and hint. Nothing counts sample points (rule 11).
  • Help. One line goes back: "On a lead card, Cover-letter points asks a model to pair what the record asks for with what your CV, entries and papers show, each line cited. It needs an account, it is model text to put in your own words, and it is never sent or added to an export."
  • Accessibility. The button is a 44 px <button type=button> with data-key cover-${id}. The busy state lives outside the card render. Focus goes to the summary after a result and back to the button after an error.
  • Fork for Dakshitha. Every lead card (recommended), or only kept cards.

Review after the build (fresh-context Opus, 2026-11-04)

  • Must-fix: "Points again" returns the stored job, because the submit key is user, brief and record, and it still spends quota. The label is untrue (rule 10).
  • Should-fix:
    • A consent 403 shows a sign-in link.
    • A timeout says "could not be made" while the job may still be running.
    • Focus falls to the body on click.
    • Polling continues after the user leaves the brief.
    • The student hint says "papers".
    • No check covers a sample record's badge.
    • Every card makes a GET on render (17 a brief), with no rate limit.
  • Nice-to-have:
    • The hint repeats under the result.
    • The hyphen in the label renders with wide spacing.
    • The screenshots need re-capturing.
    • There is no researcher card capture.
  • Industry leads: no button. The skill needs an opportunity's call text, and a company lead goes to the hand-off draft.
S45 design: showing Scout's checks in the answerdocs/design/S45_SCOUT_FLAGS_DESIGN.md, 4 Nov 2026

Design pass, 2026-11-04, for security review item S4 and S7 (docs/design/S45_SECURITY_REVIEW.md).

  • General advice. A second block under the cited answer, inside .scout-answer. Heading "General advice, not from records" with an "Uncited" tag. Plain surface and solid line border, reusing the by-code style. Line under it: "General guidance from the model. It cites no record and states no date or amount. Check details with the sponsor." Hidden when general is null.
  • Unsupported sentences. Each unsupported string found as an exact substring is wrapped in <mark class="unsupported"> with a dotted underline, a visible "?" (aria-hidden) and screen-reader text "(not confirmed by the cited record)". If a string does not match, the notice lists it instead.
  • Notices. Unsupported, not flagged: "Scout could not confirm {n} sentence(s) against the cited records. They are underlined above. Open the record before relying on them." Flagged with a body: shown above the text, "This answer did not pass the citation check twice. {withheld} sentence(s) were removed. What remains is shown, but check each claim against its record." Flagged and all withheld: the existing withheld wording only, no model tag. Reason codes are never shown.
  • The "checked" line. Unchanged when nothing is flagged. With unsupported sentences: "Written by a model. Some sentences could not be confirmed; they are marked." Flagged: "Written by a model. It failed the citation check; sentences were removed."
  • Help text. "I stop after a fixed number of tool steps for one question." Student: "A model reads your CV when you ask for cover-letter points, and when it opens a CV part to answer a question. Contact details are blanked first." Researcher: "A model reads your documents and entries when you ask for cover-letter points, or when it opens them to answer a question, with contact details blanked."
  • Forks for Dakshitha. A: inline marks with a list fallback (recommended) or a list only. B: keep unsupported sentences visible and marked (recommended) or remove them.
S43 review — student-first UI, fresh contextdocs/design/S43_REVIEW.md, 4 Nov 2026

Independent UI and UX review of Phase 7, written on 4 Nov 2026. The reviewer read docs/REBUILD_PLAN.md Phase 7, docs/design/S43_DESIGN.md, the S43 rows in docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/design/A11Y_CHECKLIST.md, the web code, the three route files and every screenshot in build/s43_walk/ and build/s43_walk_signin/. No server was run. Each finding names the screen, the place in the code, what is wrong and a fix.

Counts: 7 must-fix, 19 should-fix, 9 nice-to-have.

---

Must-fix

M1. Sign-in failures land on a raw JSON page

  • Screen: every "Sign in" link, and "Check my fit with my CV" on the landing for a signed-out visitor.
  • Where: perch/auth/routes.py callback, the except AuthError branch returns {"error": code} with status 400. /auth/login answers {"detail":"auth_unavailable"} when no identity provider is set up. build/s43_walk/w1280-debug-student-start.png shows exactly this page.
  • What is wrong: a student who presses Back at the provider, whose state cookie expired, or who visits while SSO is not registered sees a JSON blob with no way home. The plan's Risks section says Temple SSO is not registered yet, so on the demo the landing's second button may lead here every time.
  • Fix: on a browser navigation, redirect both failures to /#/ with a code, such as /#/?signin=failed or ?signin=unavailable. The app shows "Sign-in did not finish. Try again." in the banner slot, as design 2.1 says. When sign-in is unavailable, the landing shows "Try a sample student" instead of a dead sign-in link.

M2. My Perch counts sample leads together with public leads

  • Screen: My Perch, the brief rows, such as "Built 3 Nov 2026 · 12 leads · done" in w1280-my-perch.png.
  • Where: perch/user/routes.py _summary sets "leads": len(sb.leads). A student brief holds route F public leads and route S SYNTHETIC leads. web/account.js line 225 prints that number.
  • What is wrong: standing rule 11 says synthetic records never appear in any number next to public records. This count mixes them.
  • Fix: return public and sample counts apart from _summary, using lead.sample. Show "10 options" and, on its own, "10 sample options", or show only the public count. keptWords in web/student.js line 35 already does this split.

M3. The student brief describes its search falsely

  • Screen: the student brief, Your options, the Fellowships route, in w1280-brief-student.png.
  • Where: web/student.js line 11 names the route "Fellowships (public)". Line 249 says "Public listings: Temple's Scholar Development and Fellowships Advising list and NIH fellowships." But perch/service.py _run_fellowships searches every non-synthetic Scholarship row. The store now holds 360 of those, and the temple_pages scholarships are among them.
  • What is wrong: the screen names two sources when it searched three. A student who just browsed 360 Temple awards is told the brief searched fellowships only. That is a false statement on screen under rule 10. fromPage and amountText at lines 271 and 376 also treat only temple_sdfa as a page source.
  • Fix: first confirm with one brief that its F leads include source: temple_pages. If they do, rename the route "Temple awards and fellowships". Write the hint from the stage's own summary line, which already says "N Temple-listed and N NIH fellowships searched". Extend fromPage to temple_pages. If they do not, the landing's promise of checking fit against Temple awards is not met, and that is a scope question for Dakshitha.

M4. The sample route sits as a tab inside the student brief, against fork F6

  • Screen: the student brief route switch "Fellowships | Scholarships and awards, Sample data", and Compare's "Scholarships and awards (sample)" table.
  • Where: web/student.js lines 223 to 231, 244 and 398 to 449, and perch/service.py _run_scholarships.
  • What is wrong: fork F6, decided on 4 Nov, puts samples on their own screen, linked from the brief, so that rule 11 is met by layout. The build still ships option B, a sample tab beside real options. web/help.js line 297 then tells users that samples "live on their own screen", which is false for the brief.
  • Fix: for a signed-in student, drop the S stage or hide its tab, and add a "See how Perch works with sample records" link to #/samples/student. Keep the S route only for the guest's sample persona, where every record is already invented. Then the Help line becomes true. If this cannot land by the gate, put the change to Dakshitha and correct the Help line now.

M5. The walk did not measure the brief screens or dark mode

  • Screen: the researcher brief, the student brief and both Compare screens, at both widths.
  • Where: build/s43_walk/report.json holds 28 states, and none is a brief-* state. Its checks lack guest_researcher_brief, guest_sample_persona_brief and the two guest_keep_compare_* checks. scripts/ux_walk.py never calls emulate_media with a dark colour scheme.
  • What is wrong: the report's "0 axe violations" and "0 targets under 44 px" cover 14 screens in light mode only. Checklist items 1, 2 and 9 are unverified for the brief screens. The builder's own note of 20 to 40 px targets there is not checked. Phase 7 is done only when the walk is clean with axe on laptop and phone.
  • Fix: rerun the walk with the briefs flow included, and add a dark pass for every flow. Known candidates under 44 px on brief screens: .export-pop .check at 40 px in web/styles.css line 1010; the Routes .filter-chip at 36 px on a fine pointer, line 1284; the Scout owl button owl-sm at 40 px, line 454; .cite at 32 px on a fine pointer, line 1213. The probe skips checkboxes, so the export menu's 40 px rows never show up. Either fix each one or list it with a reason, as the checklist asks.

M6. The consent text promises a withdrawal the app does not offer

  • Screen: welcome, step 2, and the account page.
  • Where: perch/auth/consent.py says "You can withdraw this consent at any time." POST /me/consent/withdraw exists in perch/auth/routes.py. No screen calls it, and web/account.js shows the consent only as a fact.
  • What is wrong: a user agrees to a text that names a control they cannot reach. Rule 10 forbids stating a capability that the product does not offer. This is consent text, so the gap matters more than in other copy.
  • Fix: add "Withdraw consent" to the account page's Consent row, with a confirm that says it stops the model jobs and does not delete data. The router in web/app.js line 113 redirects any user with consent.required to the welcome screen, so after a withdrawal the account page and the public lists must stay reachable. Otherwise the user is trapped on the welcome screen.

M7. The Retry button on a failed list load throws

  • Screen: Temple awards and Research funding, the error state.
  • Where: web/browse.js lines 242 to 247. When GET /filters fails, filters stays null and the error state's Retry calls load(). params() at line 99 then reads filters.total, which throws a TypeError on the student side.
  • What is wrong: the one recovery a student is offered on a slow or failed server does nothing. The researcher side gets results back but no filter bar, because drawBar is never called.
  • Fix: make Retry rerun the whole start: fetch /filters, then drawBar(), then load(). Add a walk plant that fails /filters once and checks that Retry brings the list back.
