Should-fix

S1. Two names for one group of awards

  • Screen: awards and funding lists, the tag row.
  • Where: web/browse.js line 204 labels the chip "All Temple". The group heading from perch/browse/routes.py OPEN_LABEL, and the card tag at web/browse.js line 60, both say "Open across Temple".
  • What is wrong: "All" and "All Temple" sit side by side, and "All Temple" reads as "everything at Temple". It actually means the awards open to every school plus those with no stated scope.
  • Fix: rename the chip "Open across Temple". This matches the group heading and the card tag, and Help line 165.

S2. The phone header wraps onto two rows

  • Screen: every signed-out and guest screen at 360 px, such as w360-landing-guest.png, where "Guest" and "Sign in" drop below the wordmark.
  • Where: web/styles.css lines 1206 to 1211, the S24 phone header. Under 480 px .bar-in is a grid with three columns, .bar-tools is display: contents, and only #help and #theme are placed on row 1. The new #acct-slot has no grid place, so it falls to row 2 under the wordmark. The S43 nowrap rules at lines 1437 and 1438 have no effect on a grid.
  • What is wrong: the sticky header is about 108 px tall on a 780 px phone. It hides more of each screen and more of whatever has focus.
  • Fix: give the grid four columns, 1fr auto auto auto, and place #acct-slot in column 2 on row 1, with Help and the theme in columns 3 and 4. Delete the dead nowrap rules. Check the guest header at 360 px: wordmark, Guest chip, Sign in, Help and the theme icon on one row. Shorten "Guest" to an icon with a label if the row still overflows. Add a walk check that the header's height is under 64 px at 360 px, and prove it fails first on today's build.

S3. Focused controls can hide under the sticky header

  • Screen: all screens, most on phones.
  • Where: web/styles.css has no scroll-padding-top. .bar at line 102 is position: sticky, and the brief's .tabs-wrap at line 208 is sticky as well.
  • What is wrong: WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.4.11 asks that a focused control not be fully hidden. Shift+Tab upward can put a control under the header.
  • Fix: set html { scroll-padding-top: calc(var(--bar-h, 56px) + 8px); }, and add the tab bar's height on brief screens. Add a walk check that tabs back through a long list and asserts each focused element's top is below the header's bottom.

S4. Past deadlines look like open ones

  • Screen: Research funding with Temple only on, such as "CIBER Research Award, Closes 5 Dec 2022" in w360-funding-temple.png. The same applies to scholarship deadlines.
  • Where: web/browse.js deadlineText, lines 48 to 55. The browse route accepts closes_after, but params() never sends it.
  • What is wrong: the plan's Risks section says some Temple pages list stale dates. A student will read "5 Dec 2022" as the next deadline.
  • Fix: keep the copied date and add a code-written label "This date has passed" when the date is before today. Rule 3 allows a label derived by code. Optionally add a "Hide past dates" control that sends closes_after.

S5. The same school shows twice on a funding card

  • Screen: Research funding, Temple only, such as "Fox School of Business" twice on the CIBER card and "Liberal Arts" twice on Co-Sponsorship.
  • Where: web/browse.js lines 75 and 76. One tag comes from schools and a second from agencyShort(r.agency), which holds the same school name on a Temple page record.
  • What is wrong: it looks like a bug, and it pushes the level and the title down on a phone.
  • Fix: skip the agency tag when its text equals one of the school tags.

S6. The funding list is ordered by record id

  • Screen: Research funding. The first card is "2022 Alumni Engagement Innovation Fund-Italy" with the number "04".
  • Where: perch/store/postgres.py line 144, ORDER BY id. Design section 9 says the default order is by name.
  • What is wrong: awards look name-sorted only because their ids are built from their names. For 1,523 funding records, id order means nothing to a researcher.
  • Fix: order by the record's name or title, case-folded, with the id as a tie-break. Keep the cursor stable on that key.

S7. No way from the awards list to "Check my fit"

  • Screen: Temple awards, at both widths.
  • Where: web/browse.js lines 234 to 239. The only link onward is to the sample records.
  • What is wrong: the student's main task is to find awards that fit them. After reading the list they must go Back to the landing to find the fit flow.
  • Fix: add a quiet call to action above the first group or at the foot: "Check which of these fit your CV", linking to #/student. A guest sees "Try a sample student" instead.

S8. The sample brief says "your CV"

  • Screen: the guest's sample student brief, in w1280-brief-student.png.
  • Where: the brief's sub-line "Fellowships and sample scholarships, checked against your CV by rule" in web/app.js, and the hint at web/student.js line 250.
  • What is wrong: the banner right below says "Built from an invented SYNTHETIC student. Nothing here is about you." The two lines contradict each other.
  • Fix: when the brief is the sample persona, say "checked against the sample student's CV by rule". The same applies to "Still needed" and "your achievement A" wording on its cards.
  • A second false line: the guest start screen at web/student.js line 73 says "Nothing in it is about you, and its scholarships are invented too." The sample brief's Fellowships route holds real public listings, such as NRSA F31 and the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship. Only the sample route is invented. Say "Its sample scholarships are invented. The fellowships it checks are real public listings."

S9. Help contradicts the guest hand-off

  • Screen: Help, Your privacy, and the guest student Compare in w360-brief-student-compare.png.
  • Where: web/help.js line 274 says "Hand-offs and Scout need an account." The guest's student Compare drafts a note with "Copy the draft" and "Open in my mail app".
  • What is wrong: one of the two is false under rule 10.
  • Fix: say "Researcher hand-off drafts and Scout need an account. A student's note is written by code and works for guests too." Or remove the note for guests. Dakshitha decides which.

S10. Help leaves out the Temple award pages as a source

  • Screen: Help, How Perch works.
  • Where: web/help.js line 204 lists "OpenAlex, NIH RePORTER, NSF, Grants.gov and the Temple fellowship list."
  • What is wrong: the Temple awards list, the main student screen, comes from Temple's public school and college pages. Help does not name that source.
  • Fix: add "Temple's public scholarship and award pages". Match the words to SOURCE_WORDS.temple_pages in web/browse.js line 16.

S11. The consent text is clipped on a phone

  • Screen: welcome at 360 px, in build/s43_walk_signin/w360-welcome.png.
  • Where: .consent-text { max-height: 280px; overflow: auto } in web/styles.css line 1418.
  • What is wrong: the text stops mid-sentence and no scroll bar shows. "I agree" can be ticked without the withdrawal and 35-day lines ever being seen.
  • Fix: drop the max-height on the welcome screen. The text is eight sentences long. Split it into one paragraph per sentence, or a list, so it reads in steps.

S12. A signed-in user without consent cannot browse public lists

  • Screen: any route for a user with needs_welcome or consent.required.
  • Where: web/app.js lines 113 to 117 redirect every route except Help to #/welcome.
  • What is wrong: the awards and funding lists need no session at all, but a new account cannot reach them until it agrees to send a CV to a provider. The welcome screen also has no "Not now" or "Sign out" button, so a user who does not want to agree has only the account menu.
  • Fix: let #/awards, #/funding, #/samples and Help through without the welcome. Gate only the screens that read or store user text. Add a "Sign out" link at the foot of the welcome screen.

S13. The delete dialog under-describes, and fails badly after the key is gone

  • Screen: account, the delete dialog, in w360-delete-dialog.png.
  • Where: web/account.js line 147 for the text. web/api.js ERROR_WORDS has no delete_incomplete, which perch/user/routes.py line 129 returns.
  • What is wrong: the text names CV, entries, briefs and account. perch_delete_user_rows clears every table, including documents, kept leads and drafts, and the session ends. The dialog does not say you will be signed out. If a shred hook fails, the user's key is already destroyed, yet the dialog says "The server answered 500." and offers Delete again with no explanation.
  • Fix: use the design's list: "Your CV and entries, your briefs, your saved awards and leads, your hand-off drafts and cover points, and your account." Add "You will be signed out." Map delete_incomplete to "Your key is destroyed, so your data can no longer be read. Clean-up did not finish. Press Delete again to finish it."

S14. Policy numbers in copy have no source in the code

  • Screen: welcome, the account page, the delete dialog, the guest banner and Help.
  • Where: "35 days" appears only in perch/auth/consent.py and web/account.js. No backup config sets it yet, because backups are Phase 10. "It ends in an hour" is a fixed string in perch/auth/routes.py, not built from the session's expires_at.
  • What is wrong: a number in user-facing copy should come from the code that enforces it, in the spirit of rules 3 and 10. The 35-day claim cannot be checked today.
  • Fix: keep the contract text, but record "35 days" as UNVERIFIED in the Phase 10 runbook task, so the backup retention is set to match before release. Build the guest notice's duration from the same constant as the session TTL.

S15. Student start loses unsaved text and moves focus to the top

  • Screen: Check my fit, signed in, in build/s43_walk_signin/w360-student-start.png.
  • Where: web/student.js lines 92 and 100. Each save calls draw(), which rebuilds the whole screen with a new empty field. Line 165 then focuses the page title.
  • What is wrong: a student who pastes a CV, then types interests and presses "Save interests" loses the pasted CV. After every save, keyboard focus jumps to the heading. "Save my CV" with an empty box only announces "Paste your CV text first." to screen readers, so sighted users see nothing happen.
  • Fix: keep the textareas' values in module state across redraws, or update only the changed section. Put focus back on the button that was pressed, or on the new "is stored" line. Show the empty-box message under the field with aria-describedby.

S16. Account menu may not open links on iPhone

  • Screen: the account chip menu on a phone.
  • Where: web/app.js line 304. The menu closes on focusout when relatedTarget is outside the wrapper.
  • What is wrong: iOS Safari does not focus a link or button on tap, so relatedTarget is null. The menu may close before the tap lands, and My Perch, Account and data, and Sign out become unreachable. Playwright Chromium cannot show this. This needs a check on a real device.
  • Fix: close the menu on a pointerdown outside the wrapper and on Escape, not on focusout. Add aria-haspopup="true" while there.

S17. Error copy is written for developers

  • Screen: any screen when the server does not answer, or answers with an unmapped code.
  • Where: web/api.js line 56, "Perch's server did not answer. Check that perch serve is running." Also the fallback "The server answered 500."
  • What is wrong: a student does not run perch serve. The message tells them nothing they can act on.
  • Fix: "Perch could not be reached. Check your connection and try again." For unknown codes: "Something went wrong on Perch's side. Try again in a minute."

S18. A guest sees a live "Draft the email" button on the researcher Compare

  • Screen: the guest researcher brief, Compare, in w1280-brief-researcher-compare.png and w360-brief-researcher-compare.png.
  • Where: the hand-off section in web/handoff.js and web/app.js. web/api.js maps account_required to "guests cannot draft hand-offs", so the press can only fail.
  • What is wrong: design section 5 says a guest sees "Sign in to draft a hand-off". The button invites an action that ends in an error. The line above it also says Perch "does not save it", but hand-off drafts are now stored jobs for signed-in users.
  • Fix: for a guest, replace the button with "Sign in to draft a hand-off", linking to sign-in with the current hash. Check the "does not save it" sentence against the hand-off job code and correct it.

S19. The welcome screen rebuilds itself on every tick

  • Screen: welcome, steps 1 and 2.
  • Where: web/account.js lines 31 to 36 and 57 to 88. Each checkbox change calls draw(), which replaces the whole screen with fill(root, ...).
  • What is wrong: the checkbox the user just ticked is destroyed and rebuilt. Focus comes back through data-key, but a screen reader may lose the state change or read the page again. Text typed in the OpenAlex field survives only because it is kept in state.
  • Fix: update in place. Show or hide the OpenAlex field, and set Continue's disabled and its hint, without rebuilding the checkboxes.

Nice-to-have

N1. Route changes keep the old scroll position

  • Where: web/app.js, the awards, funding, samples and student branches of route(), have no window.scrollTo(0, 0). The list then focuses its title with preventScroll.
  • What it causes: a list can open half-way down the page. The header drawn mid-page in w360-awards-empty.png and w360-student-start.png is a capture artifact of this, not a layout bug.
  • Fix: scroll to the top on each of these routes, as the account routes do.

N2. The list title steals focus after loading

  • Where: web/browse.js lines 252 and 253 focus the title after the first load().
  • What it causes: a user who started typing in the search box while the list loaded loses their place. The focus ring around the whole title also looks like a selected box.
  • Fix: focus the title only if focus is still on body or main. Hide the outline on h1[tabindex="-1"]:focus while keeping it for keyboard focus on controls.

N3. "Up to" is added by code where the page may not say it

  • Where: web/browse.js line 44 writes "Up to $X" for any scholarship with a maximum and no minimum. web/student.js line 376 does so only for temple_sdfa.
  • What it causes: the same record can read "Up to $5,000" on the list and "$5,000" in the brief. "Up to" is a claim about the award.
  • Fix: share one amount helper. Write "Up to" only when the record's quote for the amount says so.

N4. The guest banner uses a question-mark icon

  • Where: web/app.js line 228 uses icon("help").
  • Fix: use an info icon, as design 1.3 says. A question mark suggests a link to Help.

N5. The guest banner does not show when the session ends

  • Where: web/app.js line 229 shows the fixed notice. expires_at is in the session answer.
  • Fix: add "Ends at 3:40 pm", rendered from expires_at, so a guest knows how long a brief will last.

N6. Brief rows on My Perch all read "Student brief"

  • Where: web/account.js line 224, and the raw status word "done" on line 225.
  • Fix: name the CV the brief was built from, or the top option's title. Map the status to plain words: "Ready", "Failed", "Still building".

N7. The account page has no way to add a CV

  • Where: web/account.js line 125, "You have no stored documents."
  • Fix: add a link "Add your CV" to #/student.

N8. The walk never shows a card with an explanation

  • Where: scripts/walk_server.py uses the fake model, so every brief card in the screenshots reads "The explanation was withheld because it failed the citation checks twice."
  • What it causes: the reviewer cannot judge the real card, and the withheld state looks alarming when it fills a whole page.
  • Fix: make the fake model return one valid explanation for the walk, so both states are captured. Consider softer copy for the withheld state, such as "No explanation is shown for this one. Its fields are copied from the record."

N9. The Level menu on the funding list mostly empties it

  • Where: web/browse.js lines 226 to 230. With Temple only off, choosing a level drops every federal record, because they state no level.
  • Fix: show the Level menu only when Temple only is on, as the tag row already does, or add a hint "Most federal listings state no level."

---

What works

  • Samples stay apart in the lists: /awards and /opportunities never return a sample, every sample card carries the dashed badge, and the sample screen opens with its note. The walk plants prove both checks fail first.
  • Counts come from the server: chip counts match GET /filters, and group totals come from the route.
  • "Not stated" reads honestly: missing amounts and deadlines say "Not stated" without looking broken.
  • The delete guard is sound: a real <dialog>, focus starts in the field, Escape returns focus to the opener, and Delete stays disabled until the field holds exactly delete.
  • The tag row on a phone: it scrolls inside itself with a fade, chips are 44 px, and the page has no sideways scroll on the measured screens.
S43 design — student-first UI on the v1 stackdocs/design/S43_DESIGN.md, 4 Nov 2026

Design pass for Phase 7 of docs/REBUILD_PLAN.md. This document proposes; it builds nothing. The visual language stays the S24 one in docs/design/S24_REBUILD.md: same tokens, type, shapes, sizes and motion. Only screens, states and copy change.

Gate: Thursday 5 Nov 2026, 18:00. Each item below is marked [gate] or [later].

The gate means three things work live:

  • Guest or sign-in: a visitor can sign in, or start a guest session, or just browse.
  • Temple awards: the awards list shows Temple awards with the Temple-only toggle and the school tags.
  • A brief on the cloud model: a researcher brief from an OpenAlex id builds on the cloud profile. A student brief from a stored CV is also gate if S42 lands its account route by Thursday morning. If S42 slips, the researcher brief alone meets the gate.

---

0. What the current code does that blocks this design

Read this section first. Each item is a backend change the UI cannot work around.

  • Temple-only filters on the wrong field. perch/store/postgres.py adds temple_funded to the WHERE clause when temple_only is set. In temple_awards_v1.jsonl, temple_funded is true for 4 of 285 records. A toggle built on this shows 4 awards. Fork F1 decides the fix.
  • Unstated scope turns into "external". perch/store/denorm.py maps a missing scope to external. The manifest counts 30 scholarships with scope unstated. They are listed on Temple pages, but today they would drop out of every Temple filter. Denorm must keep Temple-page records inside Temple, whatever their scope. Fork F2 decides how they are labelled.
  • School tags are cleared when scope is not "school". denorm.columns empties schools unless scope is school. So tag counts from the database will be lower than the manifest's by_school numbers. The UI must render counts from GET /filters only, never from the manifest.
  • Browse routes do not exist yet. GET /awards, GET /opportunities, GET /filters and GET /samples are in the contract, section 9.2, but no route serves them. The store's browse method exists, so each route is a thin wrapper.
  • Account routes the design needs do not exist yet. GET /me/saved, PUT /me/saved/{record_id}, DELETE /me/saved/{record_id}, POST /briefs/{id}/cover-points and GET /briefs/{id}/handoff/{draft_id} are missing. GET /me is missing too, so the account page has nothing to read.
  • The student brief has no account route yet. POST /briefs still requires an OpenAlex author_id, and request_models.py has no audience field. The student brief moves onto the account path in S42, which is running in a worktree now. S43 builds against the S42 result.
  • Guest compare contradicts guest keep. Section 7.4 says a guest can compare and export. Section 9.1 makes keep, dismiss and restore need a signed-in user. Compare works on kept leads, so a guest cannot compare. Fork F3 decides the fix.
  • GET /usage needs a user. The contract says any session. This decides whether a guest sees a budget line. The design below shows no budget to guests, so this is not a gate blocker.
  • /welcome is a server-rendered placeholder page. It is labelled PLACEHOLDER and tells the reader to POST by hand. S43 replaces it with an app screen at #/welcome. The server route should just redirect to /#/welcome.
  • Three strings on screen are now false under rule 10.
    • The footer promise "Nothing about you is stored" is false, because signed-in users' CVs are stored encrypted.
    • The header chip "Local · nothing stored" is false, because the deployment runs on the cloud profile.
    • The meta description leads with researchers only.
    • Replacements are in section 1.5.
  • Private-mode code goes away. web/mode.js, web/private.js, the Local or Cloud dialog, the "End session" button and every privApi and PRIVATE_ID branch in web/app.js are removed by S42. S43 must not rebuild any of them.

---

1. Landing

1.1 Layout [gate]

The landing keeps the owl, the headline and the 680 px column. What changes is the order: students come first.

+--------------------------------------------------+

|  Find funding that fits.                         |

|                                                  |

|  [ Check my fit with my CV ]     <- secondary    |
|  Try it as a guest. Nothing is saved.            |
+--------------------------------------------------+
| promises row                                     |
+--------------------------------------------------+
  • The control: the existing Student | Researcher segmented control stays. Student is chosen by default.
  • The student side: two buttons. "Browse Temple awards" opens the awards list and needs no session. "Check my fit with my CV" starts sign-in, or opens the student brief start screen if the user is signed in.
  • The researcher side: the existing search field with Find, plus a quiet link "Browse funding" that opens the funding list.
  • The guest line: under the buttons, one quiet line with a "Try it as a guest" link. It calls POST /auth/guest with the chosen audience.
  • The memory: a signed-in user lands on the side in last_audience. A signed-out visitor always lands on Student.

1.2 States [gate]

1.3 The guest banner [gate]

  • Where: in the existing #banner slot under the header, on every screen of a guest session.
  • Text: the string the server already sends in notice: "Nothing is saved in a guest session. It ends in an hour."
  • Action: a "Sign in" link at the end of the banner, which goes to /auth/login?return_to= the current hash.
  • Style: the chip colour background with ink text and an info icon. It is not amber, because amber means sample data.
  • Exports: a guest export carries the same text at the top, as the contract says.
  • Expiry: when a call returns 401 in a guest session, the app shows "Your guest session has ended. Nothing was saved." with Start again and Sign in buttons.

1.4 The account chip [gate]

  • What replaces the Local chip: a button with the user's display_name, or "Account" if there is none.
  • What it opens: a small menu with "My Perch", "Account and data", the side switch when the user holds both roles, and "Sign out".
  • Sign out: calls POST /auth/logout, then follows the IdP end-session URL if one comes back.

1.5 Copy replacements [gate]

  • Footer promise 1 stays: "Every claim cites a public record."
  • Footer promise 2, replacing "Nothing about you is stored": "Your CV is stored encrypted. You can delete it at any time." DRAFT for Dakshitha.
  • Footer promise 3 stays: "Hand-offs are drafts; nothing is sent."
  • Meta description: "Perch lists Temple scholarships and research funding that fit you, every claim linked to its record." DRAFT for Dakshitha.
  • Headline sub-line: "Temple scholarships and research funding, every claim linked to its record." DRAFT for Dakshitha.

---

2. Sign-in, welcome and the account page

2.1 Sign-in [gate]

  • No sign-in screen of our own: "Sign in" is a plain link to /auth/login?return_to=<current hash>. The IdP shows its own page.
  • The return: the callback lands on return_to. If needs_welcome is true, the app goes to #/welcome first and then back.
  • Errors: a failed login returns to the landing with "Sign-in did not finish. Try again." in the banner slot.

2.2 The welcome screen, #/welcome [gate]

It has two steps on one page. Both must be done before the user continues.

+----------------------------------------------+
| Welcome to Perch                             |
|                                              |
| 1. What brings you here?                     |
|  [x] I am a student      <- 56 px rows       |
|  [ ] I am a researcher                       |
|  You can pick both. You can change this      |
|  later on the account page.                  |
|                                              |
| 2. How Perch uses your CV                    |
|  (consent text, version N)                   |
|  [ ] I agree                                 |
|                                              |
|  [ Continue ]                                |
+----------------------------------------------+
  • Step 1, the side: two checkbox rows, Student and Researcher. At least one must be ticked. This calls POST /me/roles.
  • Researcher extra: if Researcher is ticked, an optional field "Your OpenAlex author id" appears, with a Find link that reuses the researcher search. This calls PUT /me/openalex. It can be skipped.
  • Step 2, consent: the full text from perch/auth/consent.py, shown as written, with its version number. An "I agree" checkbox. This calls POST /me/consent with the version.
  • Continue: disabled until both steps are done. It goes to return_to, or to the side's home.
  • The baseline consent text is the contract text. It names the provider from PERCH_CONSENT_PROVIDER_NAME. It states the blanking of contact details, encrypted storage, delete-my-data, the 12-month rule, backups clearing within 35 days, and withdrawal.
  • A proposed plainer version, DRAFT for Dakshitha:
    • "Perch sends the text of your CV and entries to {provider}, so it can write your briefs, hand-off drafts and cover points."
    • "Before any text is sent, Perch blanks emails, phone numbers and links."
    • "Your CV and entries are stored encrypted, under a key that belongs to you."
    • "You can delete all your data at any time, on the account page."
    • "If you do not use Perch for 12 months, your data is deleted."
    • "After you delete your data, backups clear within 35 days."
    • "You can withdraw this consent at any time. That stops these model jobs. It does not delete your data."
  • A changed text needs a new version. The consents row stores the hash of the exact text. If Dakshitha takes the plainer version, PERCH_CONSENT_VERSION must rise, and every existing user sees the consent step again.
  • No Temple policy is stated. The text says nothing about Temple's own data rules, because the code does not know them.

2.3 The account page, #/account [gate for delete, later for the rest]

+----------------------------------------------+
| Account and data                             |
|                                              |
| Signed in as  <display name>                 |
| Your sides    [x] Student  [x] Researcher    |
| OpenAlex id   A50... [Change]                |
| Consent       Version N, agreed. [Withdraw]  |
|                                              |
| Your documents                               |
|   CV (label)                    [Remove]     |
|                                              |
| Delete my data                               |
|   (what is deleted, the 12-month rule)       |
|   [ Delete my data... ]   <- danger button   |
+----------------------------------------------+
  • Sides: the same two checkboxes as the welcome screen, calling POST /me/roles. [later]
  • OpenAlex id: shown only to researchers. Change reuses the welcome field. [later]
  • Consent: shows the version agreed. Withdraw calls POST /me/consent/withdraw after a confirm that says it stops the model jobs and does not delete data. [later]
  • Documents: the labels from GET /me/docs, each with Remove. [gate, because the student brief needs a stored CV]
  • Delete my data: a danger button that opens a dialog. [gate]

2.4 The delete dialog [gate]

  • What it says is deleted: "Your CV and entries, your briefs, your saved awards and leads, your hand-off drafts and cover points, and your account. Your key is destroyed, so nothing stored under it can be read again."
  • What it says about backups: "Backups clear within 35 days."
  • What it says about the 12-month rule: "Even if you do nothing, Perch deletes your data after 12 months without use."
  • The confirm step: a text field labelled "Type delete to confirm". The Delete button stays disabled until the field holds exactly delete. The body sent is {"confirm": "delete"}.
  • After: the server returns 202 and ends the session. The app shows the landing with "Your data was deleted." in the banner slot.
  • Keyboard: the dialog is a real <dialog>. Focus starts on the text field. Escape cancels. Focus returns to the danger button on cancel.

---

3. The awards list and the funding list

3.1 One list component, two screens [gate]

  • Students: #/awards, served by GET /awards. Kind is scholarship.
  • Researchers: #/funding, served by GET /opportunities. Kind is opportunity.
  • Shared: both use one list module with the same filter bar, card and paging. Only the record fields on the card differ.

3.2 The filter bar [gate]

laptop
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| Temple awards                                    (n) awards  |
| [ Temple only (on) ]   [search box.........]  [Level v]      |
| [All] [All Temple] [CST 26] [Liberal Arts 23] [TFMA 21] ...> |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+

phone at 360 px
+--------------------------------+
| Temple awards        (n)       |
| [ Temple only (on) ]           |
| [search box..................] |
| [Level v]                      |
| [All][All Temple][CST 26] ...> |  <- the row scrolls inside itself
+--------------------------------+
  • Temple-only toggle: a switch with the label "Temple only". It sets temple_only. Its meaning is fixed by fork F1.
  • School tags: one chip per school from GET /filters, each with its count. The order is by count, highest first.
  • The "All" chip: clears the school filter.
  • The "All Temple" chip: shows Temple records with no school on them. Fork F2 decides its exact content.
  • Tag labels: what the schools field holds, such as "CST" or "Fox School of Business". Fork F4 decides whether short names are expanded.
  • One school at a time: the tags act as a single choice, like radio buttons. Fork F5 decides whether a school's view also shows university-wide awards.
  • A record with several schools: six records name two to four schools. Such a record appears under each of its tags.
  • Level filter: a select with "Any level", "Undergraduate", "Graduate", "Faculty", and "Several levels" for mixed. Records with no level appear only under "Any level".
  • The tag row on a phone: one line that scrolls sideways inside itself, with a fade at the right edge. The page itself never scrolls sideways.
  • The researcher side: the toggle defaults to off, because most research funding is external. The tags apply only when the toggle is on.
  • The student side: the toggle defaults to on. The contract's FilterView holds only schools and levels, so it cannot tell the page whether any scholarship is outside Temple.
  • Decided for the gate: GET /filters also returns total and temple_total. If they are equal, the student toggle is hidden and the page title reads "Temple awards". This is a small addition to the contract, listed in section 10.

3.3 The award card [gate]

Field coverage drives the card. Out of 285 records, 48 state a maximum amount, 15 state a deadline and 130 state an apply link. "Not stated" is the usual case, so the card must not look broken without them.

+------------------------------------------------+
| [CST]  Undergraduate  ·  Open to one school    |
| [Award name from the record]  (serif)     |
| "...awarded to full-time undergraduate         |
|  students majoring in..."   <- quoted sentence  |
| Amount: not stated · Deadline: not stated       |
| [Save]  [Evidence]  [Open at source ->]         |
+------------------------------------------------+
  • Top line: school tags, the audience level, and the scope line.
  • The scope line: "Open to one school" for scope school. "Open across Temple" for scope temple_wide. "Scope not stated on the page" for unstated.
  • Title: the record's name, in Newsreader, as a button that opens the evidence sheet.
  • The quote: the first eligibility sentence from field_quotes, in quotation marks. It is copied, never written by a model.
  • Facts: amount and deadline are rendered by format.js from the record fields. A missing value reads "not stated".
  • Temple-funded badge: shown only when temple_funded is true. It reads "Temple-funded".
  • Actions: Save for a signed-in user, Evidence, and "Open at source", which links to source_url.
  • Save for a guest or a signed-out visitor: the button reads "Sign in to save" and links to sign-in.
  • Sort: the default order is by name. A "Closes soonest" sort is offered, and records with no deadline go last under it.
  • The funding card: the same shape, with agency, close date and award ceiling from the opportunity fields.

3.4 Sample records [gate]

  • Own list, never mixed: sample records come only from GET /samples. They never appear in /awards or /opportunities.
  • Where: a separate screen, #/samples/student or #/samples/researcher, linked from the foot of each list by "See how Perch works with sample records".
  • Badges: every sample card keeps the S24 dashed amber border and the dashed "Sample data" badge.
  • Banner: the sample screen opens with the existing sample note: "These are invented records from a test corpus. ... Do not apply to them."
  • Evidence: the sheet for a sample record states "Source: synthetic".
  • No counts: sample records never count toward any number on the awards or funding page.

3.5 Empty, error and loading states [gate]

  • Loading: three shimmer cards.
  • No match: "No awards match these filters." with a "Clear filters" button.
  • Error: "Perch could not load the list. Try again." with a Retry button.
  • End of list: a "Show more" button that follows the cursor. It is a button, not infinite scroll, so the keyboard and the footer stay reachable.

5. Porting every researcher screen

The screens stay as S24 built them. These are the changes.

  • Find: unchanged search and candidate cards. The "Tell Perch more" panel loses the "Local only" labels. A signed-in researcher can attach a stored CV from GET /me/docs with a checkbox. A guest sees the panel without the CV box, and a line "Sign in to add your CV". [gate]
  • Find, pre-filled: a researcher with a linked OpenAlex id sees "Build my brief" as the first action on the researcher landing. [later]
  • The brief: built through POST /briefs and polled through GET /jobs/{id} and GET /briefs/{id}, as S41 wired it. The progress card stays. A failed job shows the fixed message for its error_code: consent required, quota exceeded or budget exceeded. [gate]
  • Leads, the Routes tab: unchanged cards. Keep and Dismiss work for a signed-in user. For a guest, they follow fork F3. [gate for signed-in]
  • Leads, Temple filter: the Temple-only toggle and school tags inside the brief's Routes tab. [later]
  • Compare: unchanged for a signed-in user. For a guest, it follows fork F3. [later]
  • Hand-off: now a job. Draft shows the progress line until the job ends, then the stored draft. Guests see "Sign in to draft a hand-off". [later]
  • Export: unchanged menu, minus the mask option, since masks are gone. A guest export carries the guest banner text. [gate for signed-in]
  • Scout: port only so it does not break. The tab exists for signed-in users and calls the account-backed POST /briefs/{id}/scout. Guests see "Sign in to ask Scout". Phase 8, in S44 and S45, rebuilds Scout, so S43 spends no time on its design. [later]
  • Profile: unchanged. [gate]
  • Removed: the Local or Cloud dialog, the second Cloud warning, "End session", the private bar, the mask option and every "Local only" label.

5.1 The student brief [gate]

  • Start screen, #/student: "Tell Perch about you." A signed-in student picks a stored CV or adds one with POST /me/docs, then adds interests and achievements. The button reads "Find awards that fit".
  • The privacy line on that screen, DRAFT for Dakshitha: "Your CV is stored encrypted. Contact details are blanked before {provider} reads it."
  • The guest student: the guest cannot upload a CV, by contract section 7.4. The start screen offers only "Try a sample student". This builds a brief for the SYNTHETIC persona, with the sample badge and banner.
  • The call to action for a guest: "Sign in to use your own CV", shown on the sample brief.
  • The tabs: "Your options", "What Perch read", "Compare" and "Ask Scout", as S24 built them.
  • Your options: the real Temple scholarships and public fellowships come first, with verdict chips. Sample records do not appear in this tab. Fork F6 decides where they go.

---

6. Mobile at 360 px [gate]

  • Width: every screen is checked at 360 px as well as 1280 px. The walk's phone size changes from 390 px to 360 px.
  • No sideways scroll: the page never scrolls sideways. Only the tag row scrolls inside itself.
  • Header at 360 px: the wordmark, the account chip or "Sign in", and Help. The theme button moves into the account menu for signed-in users. For a signed-out visitor it stays as an icon-only button with a label.
  • Account chip: shows the first word of the name, cut with an ellipsis at 10 characters.
  • Tap targets: every chip, toggle, checkbox row and button is at least 44 px tall. Primary buttons are 48 to 56 px.
  • Filter bar: the toggle, the search and the level select stack, each at full width.
  • Cards: the action row wraps. "Open at source" takes the full width when it wraps.
  • Dialogs: the delete dialog takes the full width minus a 16 px gutter.
  • Focus order on the lists: the toggle, then the search, then the level select, then the tag row from left to right, then the first card. Each card is title button, Save, Evidence, then Open at source.
  • Focus order on the welcome screen: Student, Researcher, the OpenAlex field if shown, the consent text region, "I agree", then Continue.
  • Focus on a tag chip off screen: focusing it scrolls it into view inside the row.
  • Focus after a filter change: focus stays on the chip pressed, and the live region announces "n awards".

---

7. The walk

7.1 Flows to add [gate]

  • Guest: landing, "Try it as a guest", the banner, the awards list, a sample student brief, and the expired-session state.
  • Sign-in: the dev Keycloak login with a SYNTHETIC test user, the welcome screen, roles, consent, then the side's home.
  • Filters: the toggle on and off, three school tags, "All Temple", the level select, Show more, and Clear filters on the empty state.
  • Delete: the account page, the dialog, a wrong word that keeps Delete disabled, the right word, and the landing after.
  • Researcher brief, signed in: the existing PI flow, now on the account path.
  • Student brief, signed in: a SYNTHETIC CV stored, the brief built, then sign out, sign in and see it under My Perch.

7.2 New checks, each proven to fail first [gate]

7.3 Checklist changes

  • Item 11, "Private mode visible at a glance": retired with private mode.
  • Item 7, the private switch half: retired. The rest of item 7 stays.
  • Item 10, no sideways scroll: now at 360 px and 1280 px.
  • Item 12, samples never unbadged: now covered by two automatic checks above, not only by hand.
  • New item 14, guest banner: every guest state.
  • New item 15, delete confirm: keyboard-reachable and guarded.

---

8. Forks for Dakshitha

Each fork has the recommendation first.

F1. What does "Temple only" mean?

  • Recommended, A: listed on a Temple page. The filter keeps records whose source is temple_pages. That gives 285 records. It matches what a student expects.
  • B: Temple-funded, as stated on the page. The filter keeps records with temple_funded true. That gives 4 records today. It is stricter, but the list is nearly empty.
  • Cost of A: the records table already has a source column, so browse can filter on source = 'temple_pages'. That is a change to the temple_only WHERE clause in postgres.py and sqlite.py, plus a test, about 30 minutes. The "Temple-funded" badge stays as a separate fact on the card.
  • A cleaner version of A, if F2 is built first: once unstated Temple records stop being stored as external, Temple only becomes scope <> 'external'. Then F1 and F2 are one fix.
  • The vector table differs: record_vectors has temple_funded and schools but no source or scope. So the Temple filter inside a brief, which is a later item, needs one more column there.

F2. Where do the 30 records with unstated scope go?

  • Recommended, A: under "All Temple", with the line "Scope not stated on the page". They stay findable, and the card says honestly what is not known.
  • B: a separate "Scope not stated" chip. It is more precise, but one more chip crowds the row on a phone.
  • C: hide them. It is the cleanest list, but it loses 30 real awards.
  • Cost of A: denorm must stop mapping unstated Temple records to external. That needs a new scope value or a flag column, and a migration, about 1 hour.

F3. How does a guest keep and compare?

  • Recommended, A: allow keep and dismiss on a guest brief, stored in its Redis result. The guest brief already lives under guest_sid_hash for one hour, so nothing new is stored.
  • B: keep only in the browser for the guest session. It needs no backend change, but compare then runs on the client and diverges from compare_rows.
  • C: no compare for guests. It is the cheapest, but the contract's can-do list would need editing.
  • Cost of A: the three keep routes accept a guest session, checked through guest_tx, about 1 hour. Not needed for the gate.

F4. How are short school names shown?

  • Recommended, A: show the stored name for the gate, and add a checked display-name map later. Names such as CST, CEHD, LKSOM, STHM, TFMA and CPH stay as they are on Thursday.
  • B: expand them now from a map in data/overrides/. Each full name must be checked against the school's own page, by rule 10. It reads better for a first-year student.
  • Cost of B: about 45 minutes to build and check 15 names. Without the check, a wrong school name is an invented fact.

F5. Does a school's view also show university-wide awards?

  • Recommended, A: yes, in two labelled groups. A Fox student sees "Fox School of Business (16)" first, then "Open across Temple (n)" below.
  • B: no, a school chip shows that school only. It is simpler, but a student who picks their school misses most of what they can apply for.
  • Cost of A: two calls per view, or one call with a flag, plus a group heading. About 1 hour. B is the gate fallback if time runs out.

F6. Where do sample records live for students?

  • Recommended, A: their own screen, linked from the foot of each list and from the brief. Rule 11 is then met by layout, not only by badges.
  • B: a third tab in the student brief, "Samples". It keeps today's shape, but a sample tab next to real awards is easy to misread.
  • Cost of A: one small screen that reuses the list component. About 30 minutes.

F7. Must consent be given at sign-up, or only before a CV is added?

  • Recommended, A: at sign-up, as the backend does now. Standing rule 1 says "one consent at sign-up", and needs_welcome already enforces it.
  • B: just in time, when a CV is first added. Browsing and saving work without it. It is a gentler start, but it needs a rule 1 wording change from Dakshitha and a backend change.
  • Cost of A: none. B costs about 1 hour plus the rule edit.

F8. Where does a user with both roles switch sides?

  • Recommended, A: in the account menu, and as a control on My Perch. It is one tap away and keeps the header small at 360 px.
  • B: a Student | Researcher control always in the header. It is always visible, but it crowds the phone header.
  • Cost of A: small, about 20 minutes, using POST /me/audience.

---

9. Routine choices, decided

  • Delete confirm: the user types delete, because the backend requires that body.
  • Banner text: the server's own notice string, so the UI and the API never disagree.
  • Banner colour: neutral chip colour, so it is not confused with the amber sample style.
  • Sign-in page: none of our own; the IdP's page is used.
  • Welcome as an app screen: #/welcome in the single page app, with the server route redirecting to it.
  • Default sort on lists: by name, because only 15 of 285 records state a deadline.
  • Paging: a Show more button, not infinite scroll.
  • The quote on a card: the first eligibility sentence from field_quotes, copied as is.
  • Counts: always from GET /filters, never from the manifest.
  • Guest My Perch: not offered; a sign-in prompt instead.
  • Theme button on a phone: moves into the account menu for signed-in users.
  • Help: each changed screen gets its Help section rewritten in S43, with each claim checked against the code. The rest of Help is rewritten later.

---

10. Must-have for the gate, in build order

  1. Backend, F1: fix the temple_only filter.
  2. Backend, F2: keep unstated Temple records inside Temple.
  3. Backend: GET /awards, GET /opportunities, GET /filters and GET /samples as thin wrappers over browse. GET /filters also returns total and temple_total.
  4. Backend: the /welcome server route redirects to /#/welcome.
  5. Header: the account chip or Sign in; the Local chip and End session removed.
  6. Landing: Student first, the two student buttons, the researcher search, and the guest line.
  7. Guest: POST /auth/guest, the banner on every guest screen, and the expired state.
  8. Welcome screen: roles, consent with the contract text, Continue.
  9. Awards list: the toggle, the tags, "All Temple", the level select, the card, and the states.
  10. Funding list: the same component on opportunities.
  11. Samples screen: its own list, badged.
  12. Researcher brief: on the account path, with Find, Profile, Routes, keep for signed-in users, and export.
  13. Student brief: stored CV, built on the cloud model; the guest sample persona. This is gate only if S42 lands the account route by Thursday morning. If it does not, the researcher brief alone meets the gate.
  14. Account page: documents and delete-my-data with the dialog.
  15. My Perch, Briefs tab only: so a returning user sees past briefs.
  16. Copy: the footer, the meta description and the sub-line.
  17. Walk: the new flows and the checks in 7.2, each failing first.

Later, after the gate

  • Saved awards and leads.
  • Hand-off drafts as jobs, and the Drafts tab.
  • Cover points in the UI.
  • Guest keep and compare, fork F3.
  • School groups in a school view, fork F5, if B shipped for the gate.
  • Expanded school names, fork F4.
  • The Temple filter inside the brief's Routes tab.
  • Scout's redesign, which belongs to Phase 8.
  • Sides, OpenAlex link and consent withdrawal on the account page.
  • The rest of the Help rewrite.
QA cycle 5 (round 5, the last of the final QA cycles)docs/design/qa/CYCLE_5.md, 1 Nov 2026

How it was done

This was a black-box acceptance test on 1 Nov 2026, from 06:48 to 08:05, of the build on main at ca0c7fb. All the work ran on the dev server (port 8091), restarted on that commit at 06:48 with build/devdemo/serve.sh. The demo server (port 8090) was not tested. Cloud was never turned on: its dialog was opened and cancelled, and no script posts to the cloud switch. Three testers worked in parallel: one on Scout by API, one on exports, hand-offs, notes, Help and privacy, and one in the browser on the demo script and every screen. Answer times below are under that load unless marked quiet.

Machine checks:

  • make test ran twice. Each run passed 377 tests.
  • The full walk (scripts/ux_walk.py, axe 4.10.2) covered 214 states. It found 0 errors, 0 axe violations and 0 sideways scroll. 84 targets under 24 px are the hidden file inputs and inline text links, as in round 4.
  • make package built perch-0.1.0-ca0c7fb.zip (27.6 MB, 431 files). It opens and tests clean. Its listing holds no review shots, dev store, .env or local notes, and a scan of the extracted tree found no local path, email, tunnel host or session link.

Demo rehearsal (scripts/demo_rehearsal.py, three fresh sessions per flow):

  • --kept top2 (the demo): 15 of 15 (researcher 9 of 9, student 3 of 3, persona-1 documents 3 of 3).
  • --kept none: 15 of 15.
  • --kept weak2: 15 of 15.
  • One more top2 run on a quiet server: questions 1 to 3 took 5, 5 and 6 seconds.
  • The three demo answers were word for word the same in the three top2 sessions, the laptop run and the phone run. The model runs at temperature 0, so repeated runs are close to one sample; the kept-lead variants are the real spread.
  • The rehearsal asks only the scripted questions. G2 to G4 and G12 are off-script questions it does not ask.

Truncation: 1,706 calls in the demo Ollama journal since 06:48. Calls with "truncated" above 0: 0. The largest call was 6,773 of 8,192 tokens.

Browser and settings: Playwright Chromium. Phone 390 × 844 and laptop 1280 × 860, light and dark. 200% (640 × 430 at scale 2), 400% (320 × 215 at scale 4) and 320 × 640 reflow. Keyboard-only through the researcher flow. Back, Forward, reload and End session on every tab. Two briefs built at once. 83 screenshots are in build/review/qa5/; each one cited below was opened and looked at. The text of every screen was dumped and read beside its screenshot.

Audiences: PI-4 (A5026494099), the demo researcher; PI-9 (A5108616139), a live build by id, text only; the SYNTHETIC students persona-ug, persona-masters and persona-phd; and the SYNTHETIC researcher persona-1 on the documents-only path.

Scout: 51 API conversations, 255 questions, each in a fresh session, including twelve-turn conversations for PI-4 and persona-phd typed as professors and students type, and the budget stop. Plus the demo questions in the browser twice and the example questions once. Transcripts, aliased, are in build/review/qa5/scout/ (turns numbered from 1). Under load the median answer took 17 s, the slowest 50 s. A wrong-record check ran over every answer: 703 citation checks on 617 lines in 237 answers; 32 lines were flagged and read; 1 line, the same in 3 runs, cites the wrong record (G7).

Content checks: every export (Markdown, print page, JSON) for PI-4, the three students and persona-1, students and persona-1 masked and unmasked; every hand-off and note; every mail link decoded; about 145 Help claims checked against code or a live response. Aliased copies are in build/review/qa5/exports/.

Counts: 5 must-fix, 12 should-fix, 6 could-fix. Of 107 earlier items, 99 pass, 6 fail (T6, T10, T17, F3, F15, F16, all Scout questions off the demo script; each has a must-fix row: G2, G3, G4, G12), 1 was dropped in round 3 (T19) and 1 is left for S32 (F28).

Regression on rounds 1 to 4

Scout rows give how many runs were checked. Most Scout rows were run three times by API in fresh sessions.

G1
Routes cards (documents-only brief)
Your documents: add persona-1's CV, draft proposal and unpublished work, with no OpenAlex id. Build. Look at the first card. Its reasons start open.
Raw citation keys show in the card text. The findings read "…detect prodromal Parkinson's gait change [proposal]." and "…early gait instability [manuscript]." The Inference ends "…contributions to Parkinson's research [HT942526PRPIIRA, proposal, manuscript]." Every card on this brief does it. The same card says "cites 2 papers and documents" and "From the researcher's papers and documents", but persona-1 has no papers; both cited items are documents. The Match pill says "how closely the listing's text matches the papers". Root cause, read from GET /private/brief: the lead's cited_ids hold private:proposal and private:manuscript, but the model text cites the short keys proposal and manuscript. segments in web/format.js draws a bracket group as chips only when every id in it is in cited_ids, so the whole group stays as text; the finding lines print their text raw. The exports, hand-offs and Scout answers for the same session hold no such key (checked), so only the cards are wrong. No walk check reads card text on this path.
Document citations show as the lock chip ("Draft proposal (private)"), or are dropped where the finding already names the document. The card's own id is dropped, as on other cards. The hint reads "cites 2 documents" and the heading "From your documents" when no paper is cited. On a documents-only brief the Match line says "matches your documents".
Everyone at the demo. The persona-1 documents path is in the demo script, and its reasons start open. Raw keys read as a bug.

Strip a trailing "[proposal]" from a finding whose document is already named above it. Choose the hint and heading by whether any cited item is a paper, and the Match line by whether the brief has papers. Add a walk check that no card text on the persona-1 brief holds "[", and prove it fails first.

G6
Help, the Local / Cloud dialog, the cloud warning
Read Help on Scout and the model dialog. Read perch/scout/__init__.py lines 31 to 37 and perch/private/session.py _spec.
Help says Scout "always runs on a local model" and that Scout "always stays local"; the warning (routes.py) and the dialog (web/app.js) say the same. In code, only Scout's own reasoning model is fixed to local. Its explain_fit and draft_handoff tools use the session's fit_spec and handoff_spec, which return the cloud model when Cloud is on. These calls are not counted by take_cloud; the per-session cost cap bounds them. The text sent is what the warning already lists, so this is not a leak; it is a wrong sentence about where text goes. Not tested live: Cloud was never turned on.
One true sentence in all four places: "Scout's own model is local. With Cloud on, the fit explanations and drafts it asks for use the cloud model, and Steps marks them Cloud." Or keep Scout's two tools on local models.
Anyone weighing Cloud for a session; privacy-minded faculty.
code read; perch/private/session.py lines 77 to 90
Either fix the wording, or pass the base (local) specs to Scout's tools.
S

Behaviour unchanged, as decided. Was: fix the words, not the behaviour: Scout's own reasoning stays local; with Cloud on, its fit and draft steps use the cloud model, are counted in the session budget and are labelled Cloud on the step card; Help, the dialog and the warning say so

Ready to demo?

Nearly. The scripted researcher flow is solid: the three demo questions passed 45 of 45 rehearsal runs, gave the same answers on laptop and phone, and every page, export and hand-off on the script reads correctly, with numbers copied from records. Fix G1 first, because raw keys such as "[proposal]" show on the persona-1 documents cards that the script opens; G2 to G4 and G12 are Scout regressions on questions an audience member might type, and the presenter should steer around them if they are not fixed by the freeze.

What the presenter should know:

  • Waits: with nothing else running the three demo questions took 5, 5 and 6 seconds. A live researcher brief took 41 s this round beside another build, and 36 s on a quiet server in round 4. Under load the same questions took 10 to 40 seconds, and a second brief waits in line first (72 s this round).

  • persona-1's top lead closes 6 Nov 2026, Demo Day itself. On the day it is due, and a refreshed store may drop it, so check the persona-1 brief on the morning of the demo.
  • Scout's budget: about 14 questions in one conversation. After that, press "Start a new conversation and ask again".
  • Questions to avoid in Scout until G2 to G4 and G12 are fixed: "largest award", "largest ceiling" and "which pays most"; F31 deadline follow-ups for the PhD persona; start-over phrases other than plain "start over" (use the New conversation button); misspelt month questions such as "befor june".
  • Cloud: never turn it on during the demo. It is paid, and the wording in G6 is not yet right.
  • Exports: a student export is about 29 printed pages; show the researcher export instead.

Fix round (Perch-dev, 2026-11-01)

Of the 23 findings, 21 are done and 2 are partly done (G21, G23); none was dropped. G10 did not reproduce fresh (3 of 3 ran the right date), but a pytest showed the code gap, so it was fixed. Each Decision cell names its commits and the check that failed before the fix. The commits are aaae3fe (G5), 9649c84 (G1 and the Scout group), 83078a4 (G4's code-made call), 01cacfe (words, exports, focus), 8719c7e (G7's rehearsal check, G18, G23), 0aa20f8 (G13 on the brief's own path, G23), 1720408 (G23), 34e070c (two false rejections the bench found) and 2a65ba9 (two over-wide checks a review found: an expiry beside a close date, and "highest scoring leads" read as an amount question).

Root causes of the four regressions:

  • G2 (T6, F16): the sort was right. The brief's ceiling sort already put 25-543 first and Expeditions last. The model named the row with the biggest dollar figure. Round 4's floor check let "starting from $15,000,000" through, because "from" names a floor. The brief search also ignored top.
  • G3 (T17, F3): round 4's one clause function reached the cards, exports, note and student search rows, but not get_record. That tool handled placeholder dates and not expiries, so the expiry reached the model as close_date. A "deadline" answer then stayed in the conversation's history.
  • G4 (T10, F3): the send-back did fire on turns 6 and 13; each exchange now shows nudged. The model refused a second time. The nudge now names the exact call, and code makes that call if the model refuses again.
  • G12 (F15): the rules said "pays the most" sorts by amount, but no code made it so. The model compared the kept two, or chose fellowships only mid-conversation. Code now sets the sort and, for students, the route, and refuses compare unless the question says kept.

Live checks on the dev server, local model, three fresh runs per question:

  • G2: 9 of 9 named 25-543, up to $12,000,000 (fresh, two weak grants kept, and "largest award"). Before: 9 of 9 named Expeditions.
  • G3, G4, G12 in the long persona-phd conversation: 3 of 3. "There is no deadline stated in the record ...; the announcement expires 7 May 2028". "f31?", "drop the samples" and "whats the deadline for the f31" each ran search_options. "Which one pays most" listed the samples with their amounts.
  • G7: 3 of 3 cite PA-25-424 for the F33 line. G9: 3 of 3. G10: 3 of 3. G11: 3 of 3 ("a further lead not on the brief"). G13: 3 of 3, no forecast. G18: 3 of 3. G20: 3 of 3. G23: "what can i apply for" in brief order 3 of 3; one company id form 3 of 3; the samples count 0 of 3.
  • Exports, live: the persona-ug student export went from 1,391 to 409 lines and persona-phd's from 1,297 to 407. No forecast, no "Deadline: Expires", no bare masked findings, and no award horizon in the documents export.

How it was done

This was a black-box test on 1 Nov 2026, from 03:50 to 04:40, of the build on main at 2db76a2. All the work ran on the dev server (port 8091). The demo server (port 8090) was not tested. Cloud was never turned on: no script posts to the cloud switch.

Server: the dev server had started at 03:13, before commit fc23ff9 (03:21, student tools). It was restarted on main at 03:51 with build/devdemo/serve.sh, so every result below is on the current code. It is still running on that build.

Machine checks:

  • make test ran twice. Each run passed 358 tests.
  • The full walk (scripts/ux_walk.py, axe 4.10.2) covered 207 states. It found 0 errors, 0 axe violations and 0 sideways scroll.
  • The walk found 84 targets under 24 px. They are the 1 × 1 hidden file inputs and inline text links, as in round 3.
  • No animation looped with reduced motion. The "Task was destroyed" lines in the walk log are Playwright teardown noise.
  • The walk ran while Scout conversations and builds ran beside it. It still passed.

Demo rehearsal (scripts/demo_rehearsal.py, three runs each):

  • --kept top2 (the demo): researcher 9 of 9, student 3 of 3.
  • --kept none: researcher 9 of 9, student 3 of 3.
  • --kept weak2: researcher 9 of 9, student 3 of 3.
  • One more --kept top2 run with nothing else on the server: 3 of 3, at 5, 6 and 6 seconds.
  • The rehearsal passes demo question 2 even though every answer lists records outside the brief (F1). Its check only looks at cited ids that are brief leads. The pass counts are not evidence that questions 1 and 2 read well.
  • The model runs at temperature 0, yet runs of one conversation did not always agree. Question 1 said "your" in some runs and "the researcher's" in others.

  • The prescribed grep -ci truncat gives 955. That count is every "truncated = 0" line, one per model call, so it is not a truncation count.
  • Calls with "truncated = 1": 0 of 955. Lines with "truncating": 0.

Browser and settings:

  • Playwright Chromium on a phone (390 × 844) and a laptop (1280 × 860), in light and dark.
  • Zoom at 200% (640 × 430 at scale 2) and 400% (320 × 215 at scale 4), and 320 px reflow (320 × 640).
  • Keyboard-only through the researcher flow, with a check that every focus stop shows a ring, is on screen and is not covered.
  • 104 screenshots are kept in build/review/qa4/. Each one cited below was opened and looked at.
  • The Scout transcripts are in build/review/qa4/scout/ (one JSON per conversation, turns numbered from 1), and the exports, hand-offs and notes in build/review/qa4/exports/. Researchers in them are aliased.
  • One set of screenshots of a name-searched researcher showed a real name in the brief heading. The alias helper only knows names already in the store. Those screenshots and their text were deleted, and the evidence for F20 is a shot of the card alone.

Audiences:

  • PI-4 (A5026494099), the demo researcher.
  • PI-8 (A5067949026), found by name search, which gave two Temple matches. Its brief was built live.
  • PI-9 (A5108616139), built live by id to time a build with nothing else running.
  • PI-6 and PI-7 are not found by name; their latest institution in OpenAlex is likely not Temple. Help says to use the ORCID iD then.
  • The SYNTHETIC students persona-ug, persona-masters and persona-phd, and the SYNTHETIC researcher persona-1 (documents only).

Demo script: the whole flow was run on a laptop in light mode and again on a phone, with the text of every screen dumped and read beside its screenshot. It covered landing, find, build, Routes, the fold, the NSF chip, two Evidence records and a paper record, Keep two, Compare, the hand-off, Export Markdown, Profile, the three Scout questions, and the persona-ug student door through to the note and one Scout question.

Scout:

  • 12 API conversations: PI-4 A (15 turns, two kept, with a Stop), B (12 turns, nothing kept, typed as a professor types), C (9 turns, weak two kept), D (the four example chips), F (6 turns); persona-phd (13 turns, with a Stop and "start over"); persona-ug (7 turns, weak two kept) and one T10 run; persona-masters (3 turns); persona-1 (6 turns, G, then two more runs of the hand-off, H1 and H2).
  • Browser conversations: the demo questions twice, one run to the budget stop and past it, one run for the count question and "start over", one persona-1 hand-off.
  • 79 API answers were scanned for leaked reasoning text ("thought", a think block, CJK characters). None was found.

Content checks:

  • Every export (Markdown, print page and JSON) for PI-4, persona-ug, persona-masters, persona-phd and persona-1. Students and persona-1 were exported masked and unmasked. PI-4 holds no documents, so it has no masked export.
  • Every hand-off (grants and industry, masked and unmasked for persona-1) and both student notes.
  • Each export was scanned for ISO dates, OpenAlex work ids, private: ids and persona canaries. None was found. The only canaries in the JSON exports are the sample-record canaries, which rule 11 requires.

Timing with nothing else running: the three demo questions took 5, 6 and 6 seconds. A live build of PI-9 by id took 36 seconds, and the documents-only persona-1 build took 37 seconds. Under load the same questions took 20 to 80 seconds, and the PI-8 name build took 160 seconds, most of it "Waiting in line" behind other builds.

Counts: 7 must-fix, 10 should-fix, 11 could-fix. Of 79 earlier items, 75 pass, 3 fail (R9, T10, T17), and 1 was dropped in round 3 (T19).

Triage (Perch-dev, 2026-11-01, under Dakshitha's delegation)

All 28 findings are fix (F28 in S32). F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F7, F11, F12 and F14 carry decisions. The rehearsal script is extended as F1 and F2 say, plus a persona-1 documents-session hand-off run that checks F7, and must pass 9 of 9, 3 of 3 and 3 of 3 before the Scout items close.

Checked and fine

  • Landing, Find and pick: the id, the lower-case id, the OpenAlex URL and spaced ids all find PI-4. A name search with two Temple matches shows both with their institution and counts, and nothing runs until one is picked. A surname search gave three Temple matches.
  • Build wait: a live build shows "Waiting in line" with a plain reason when another brief is building, then steps and a bar. With nothing else running, live builds took 36 and 37 seconds.
  • Routes: five open cards and the fold; the agency and code chips count correctly ("NSF 7", "NIH 2"); bands and labels follow Help; relative times read correctly ("in 11 months", "in about 3 years").
  • Evidence: the deadline note comes first, the placeholder date is labelled, the source and fetch time show, and Escape returns focus to the title.
  • Compare and hand-off (laptop): cells, offices and the note under the table are right. The PI-4 hand-off reads well as an office would read it: the opening names the work and the two programs, then the code-written list, the papers and the note.
  • Industry: the research-security line, the "not verified" note, citing works first; the industry hand-off says "cite 2 of my papers".
  • Exports: no ISO dates, no work ids, no private ids, no persona canaries; banners equal their withheld lines; dismissed counts and footers are right; masked exports carry labels only.
  • Student door: the sample banner and badges everywhere; "Local only · nothing stored"; samples apart from public fellowships in the options, Compare, the shortlist, the notes and every Scout answer; the notes read well and say "SAMPLE DATA, A DEMONSTRATION: DO NOT SEND".
  • Privacy: Your documents and Help agree on what is kept, for how long, and who runs the server. Uploads of the wrong kind or empty files each give one plain sentence naming the file.
  • Session: End session asks first and lists what it drops; after it, Back and reload stay on the start page. Reload keeps a live brief, after the browser's leave prompt. Back and Forward move between tabs.
  • Keyboard: Find, pick, Build, Keep, Compare, Draft and Copy are all reachable by Tab, each with a visible ring.
  • Dark mode: Routes, Evidence, Compare, Profile and Industry on laptop and phone have no contrast or layout problems seen, and 0 sideways scroll.
  • Help: every number checked against code holds: the 5-year half-life, 60/40 and 50/30/20 shares, the 0.05 sponsor bonus, the 8-call cap, 120,000 tokens, 30 minutes idle, and the Match bands with the back-test basis in the decisions log.
  • Scout guard rails: the injection was refused 3 of 3; no reasoning text leaked; Stop ended a question with no answer and the next question worked; "Start a new conversation" works.

UNVERIFIED

  • Whether the "Open in my mail app" link opens a real mail client with the subject and body. Long drafts (over 1,800 characters) open with "(The draft from Perch is copied. Paste it here.)" by design; no mail client was available.
  • Whether Temple's Scholar Development and Fellowships Advising office advises graduate students, as the PhD note assumes. Its page in the note is on undergraduate.temple.edu.
  • How the demo Ollama unit behaves with two parallel slots (commit 2db76a2). This round tested the dev server against the running unit as it is.
  • Screen-reader output was not listened to; only names and roles were read from the DOM.

Ready to demo?

Not as it stands. The pages, exports, privacy, keyboard use and rules 3 and 11 hold up, and 75 of the 78 earlier fixes still in force stayed fixed. But the first two scripted Scout questions each show a visible flaw in every run, a sentence that ends "aims of." (F2) and a list of unrelated programs (F1), and Scout's hand-off on a documents brief invents published papers under a "Code, no model" label (F7). These, with F3 to F6, are small or medium fixes. After them, the rehearsal should check that every cited id in question 2 is a brief lead and that no sentence ends in a preposition, and then be run three times in a fresh session.

Fix round (Perch-dev, 2026-11-01)

All 27 findings for this round are done; F28 is left for S32. Each Decision cell names its commits and the check that failed before the fix. The rehearsal checks went in first (761427a). Most fixes then landed in two grouped commits, one for the server (a8fb295) and one for the web app (7a82d8a), because the items share files. Follow-ups found live are 383e26b, 4916ca7 and e93d5be.

Rehearsal (scripts/demo_rehearsal.py, extended as the triage asked):

  • Before any fix:
    • top2: researcher 4 of 9 (Q1 1 of 3, Q2 0 of 3, Q3 3 of 3), student 3 of 3, persona-1 0 of 3.
    • none: researcher 3 of 9, student 3 of 3, persona-1 0 of 3.
    • weak2: researcher 4 of 9, student 3 of 3, persona-1 0 of 3.
  • After the grouped fixes: 15 of 15 on each variant.
  • On the last Scout commit (383e26b), with a fresh server: top2, none and weak2 each 15 of 15. That is researcher 9 of 9, student 3 of 3 and persona-1 3 of 3.
  • Persona-1: every draft opened with code, named the lead and the documents by kind, and held no bracket.

Root causes of the three regressions:

  • F3 (T17): the expiry rule lived in two places, datefmt.closes and the cards. The export, the student export, the hand-off list, the note and the student tool each wrote the date their own way. One clause function now serves them all.
  • F4 (R9): the student export never passed the card's own id to name_papers. It also never exported the fit sentence.
  • F6 (T10): the search rows had no reason in them. The note sent the model to explain_verdict for each option.
  • F7: Scout's draft_handoff called the skill without the session's documents, so the withholding rule never ran.

Live checks on the dev server, local model, three runs each:

  • F5: the three count questions all answered from code-written counts.
  • F6: persona-ug and persona-masters, 3 of 3 each.
  • F3: "f31?" said the announcement expires, 3 of 3.
  • F10: "r01?" said none is on the brief, 3 of 3.
  • F15: "the first one" meant the last list's first, 3 of 3. "Pays the most" sorted by amount.
  • F16: the largest-ceiling question late in a conversation. The first three runs found the cut-before-sort bug, fixed in 383e26b. Three runs after it named Mid-scale Research Infrastructure-1, with a $19,999,999 ceiling. None was withheld.
  • F22: "anything from NSF" read "Proposals accepted anytime".

Machine checks:

  • make test: 377 passed.
  • Truncation: no call in the demo Ollama journal since 04:43 has "truncated" above 0. That covers about 1,550 calls since 05:11. The largest call was 6,180 tokens, against 7,076 before this round.
  • Private canary: scripts/private_canary.py ran against the dev settings and store, with Cloud not offered, after a8fb295 and again on 5753a65, after the last export change. Both runs came back ok. No canary was found in data, /tmp or the journals, and no data file changed.
  • Scout bench (bench/results/scout_qa4/, Gemma, local): 27 of 28 on round 3's tasks, against 25 of 28 in round 3. The one miss is c01, as before. The new task b06, how many papers a company cites, passed 1 of 1.
  • Full walk, first run: 213 states. It found 3 errors, all fixed in e93d5be:
    • On a phone, the New conversation button wrapped the ask row and lifted the question box.
    • The F14 check read the screen-reader prefix.
  • Rerun of the checks and ux-scout flows: 19 states, 0 errors.
  • Full walk on the last commit (e93d5be): 214 states, 0 errors, 0 axe violations, 0 sideways scroll. No animation loops with reduced motion.

For round 5:

  • Wrong record cited: persona-masters' not-eligible answer cited the F31 record for the F33 line, in 3 of 3 runs. The validator checks that an id exists, not that it is the record the sentence names.
  • Largest award: "which one pays most" once called Expeditions' floor ("from $15,000,000") the largest award. Its record states no ceiling.
  • Export length: the student export lists every not-eligible option with its rule lines, so it is still about 1,400 lines. The order now follows the screen.
  • F20: checked on PI-8's card only by DOM text and a deleted crop, because the alias helper does not know PI-8.
  • F2, a narrow reading: the decision says the card's own citation is never dropped. It becomes "this opportunity" only where it stands as a noun, after a preposition or article. Elsewhere it is still dropped, as in "aligns with dynamics [26-519].", where the sentence is whole without it.
  • Dark mode: the error hint under an empty Find and the Scout table use colour tokens that have dark values, but no walk flow shows either one in dark.
  • Commits: most items landed in two grouped commits rather than one commit per item.
QA cycle 3 (round 3 of the final QA cycles)docs/design/qa/CYCLE_3.md, 1 Nov 2026

How it was done

This was a black-box test on 1 Nov 2026 of the build on main at d342fed. All the work ran on the dev server (port 8091). The demo server (port 8090) was not tested. Cloud was never turned on: its dialog was opened and cancelled, and no script posts to the cloud switch.

Machine checks:

  • make test ran three times. Each run passed 340 tests with ruff clean, so the flaky test did not show. The three runs overlapped the walk.
  • The full walk (scripts/ux_walk.py, axe 4.10.2) took 15 minutes and covered 203 states. It found 0 errors, 0 axe violations and 0 sideways scroll.
  • 48 targets were under 24 px. All 48 are the 1 × 1 hidden file inputs.
  • 165 focus steps in 7 tab traces all showed a ring. No animation looped with reduced motion.
  • The "Task was destroyed" lines in the walk log are Playwright teardown noise, not app errors.

Browser and settings: Playwright Chromium on a phone (390 × 844) and a laptop (1280 × 860), in light and dark. Zoom was 200% (640 × 430 at scale 2) and 400% (320 × 215 at scale 4). The zoom contexts carried the session, so every brief tab was reached; round 2 reached only the landing page and Help.

Audiences:

  • PI-4 (A5026494099) is the demo researcher. It was found by id, lower-case id, OpenAlex URL and Find edge cases.
  • The SYNTHETIC students persona-ug, persona-masters and persona-phd.
  • The SYNTHETIC researcher persona-1, documents only.

Demo script: the likely Demo Day flow was run end to end on a laptop in light mode and again on a phone. That covered PI-4, Routes, the NSF chip, the fold, two Evidence records, Keep two, Compare, the hand-off, the Markdown export, the three scripted Scout questions, and the persona-ug student door. The text of every screen was dumped and read beside its screenshot.

Scout: these were the conversations run.

  • Three ten-turn PI-4 conversations by API: two leads kept, nothing kept, and two grants plus two companies kept.
  • One twelve-turn PI-4 conversation in the browser.
  • One ten-turn persona-ug conversation with a Stop.
  • Five-turn persona-masters and persona-phd conversations, each with a filter change and a Stop.
  • Every Scout row below gives its run count.

Content checks: these were done on text.

  • Every export (Markdown, JSON and print) for PI-4, persona-ug and persona-1, masked and unmasked.
  • Every hand-off and student note, and both mail links (each clicked with an edited subject and body).
  • A script checked every number and date in 70 model texts and every Scout answer against the brief's records. A question's own date echoed back is not counted as a breach.
  • A second script scanned every export, hand-off and note for 8-word phrases and canaries from the persona files.

Screenshots: about 130 working screenshots were taken. The 10 cited below are in build/review/qa3/, and each one was opened and looked at.

Counts: 7 must-fix, 12 should-fix, 9 could-fix. 47 of 50 earlier items pass. Q5 and Q20 fail, and R14 is UNVERIFIED. R17 passes with a gap in the Compare cell.
